14:I[44692,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/08cykig6vtx_p.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/07qi2okp-.yp9.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0frujd.eyhz4o.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0n4z.7yu76je-.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/09-o.77-p0p36.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/1304s0wcp2kce.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0j1uy9t~zxcf0.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/14_5o-nbg8k_r.js"],"DailyView"]

a9:I[97367,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/08cykig6vtx_p.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/07qi2okp-.yp9.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0frujd.eyhz4o.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0n4z.7yu76je-.js"],"ViewportBoundary"]
ab:I[97367,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/08cykig6vtx_p.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/07qi2okp-.yp9.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0frujd.eyhz4o.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0n4z.7yu76je-.js"],"MetadataBoundary"]
15:T813,方法上有两个核心动作。第一是目标构造。作者没有直接沿用父 subword tokenizer 的所有切分，而是围绕 grapheme cluster 设计了两类监督：一种是 every-cluster target，即保留每个 grapheme 边界；另一种是 retained-parent target，即只保留那些本来就与 grapheme 边界重合的父 tokenizer 切分。这样做的原因很明确：grapheme 边界是跨编码可表示的、对 span-preserving edit 稳定，而且正好能把“编码是否在首符号暴露了 cluster continuation 所需信息”这个问题单独拎出来。第二是编码设计与对照。作者采用已有的 UBE（Universal Byte-Level Encoding）：对 1-byte 和 2-byte UTF-8 标量保持不变，对更长的标量改写成 UTF-16 little-endian 的两个字节。这样对原本需要 3-byte UTF-8 的 codepoint，首个符号从 UTF-8 的‘4 个高位 + 长度前缀’变成了‘8 个低位’，在同一 256-codepoint page 内通常足以直接区分具体字符。为了把“更短序列”与“字节顺序”拆开，作者又构造了 UBE-BE：路由方式和总长度与 UBE 相同，但把 UTF-16 code unit 内部字节顺序反过来。这样如果 UBE 好、UBE-BE 不好，就能说明收益不是简单来自 stream 变短，而是来自 low byte first 让判别信息更早出现。

实验对象是小型 causal boundary predictor，在 matched FineWeb-2 文本上训练，在 FLORES-200 的多语种面板上评估。作者把错误分成 scalar ends 上的平衡误差，以及 scalar 内部的 false cuts；后者可以用规则 mask 去掉，不改变 scalar end 的判定，因此主分析集中在真正有意义的边界决策上。论文还构造了一个很强的诊断实验：找出那些左上下文完全相同、下一个 scalar 落在同一 256-codepoint page、但边界决策相反的成对样本。对这类样本，若编码首符号不携带足够信息，模型再怎么学也无法在一符号 lookahead 下全对；这使得“可学性”与“表示可区分性”被清楚地分开了。16:T773,最关键的结果有三组。第一，在 17 种语言的 FLORES-200 面板上，针对 every-cluster target、只允许 one-symbol lookahead 时，UTF-8 在 scalar ends 上的 balanced error 是 8.76%，UBE 降到 0.06%，而同长度控制 UBE-BE 仍有 8.62%。这个结果很硬，因为它几乎直接说明收益来自字节顺序，而不是仅仅因为 UBE 把 3-byte UTF-8 压成了 2 个符号。第二，在作者构造的 17,204 对“相同左上下文但应作相反决策”的样本上，UBE 的训练后预测器在每个 seed 都能全部答对；UTF-8 和 UBE-BE 做不到，因为两者在关键位置看到的首符号相同，信息先天不足。第三，在 Korean 和 Chinese 这类 grapheme 边界基本等于 scalar end 的语言里，问题不再是 cluster continuation，而是 retained-parent task 中“哪些字符边界要保留为 subword 边界”。在 one-symbol lookahead 下，UBE 相对 UTF-8 的总 retained-parent error 分别下降 72.91% 和 35.29%；在另外 8 个脚本上，下降幅度在 67.32% 到 99.55% 之间。作者还指出，当某脚本主要 Unicode block 落在单一 256-codepoint page 内时，UBE-BE 与 UTF-8 会比较接近，这与“low byte first 在页内直接暴露字符身份”的机制一致。

另一个很有价值的部分是对已发布 byteification 模型的审计。作者检查了 Bwen-8B（Qwen3-8B-Base 的 Bolmo-style 转换），发现它在 18 个高碎片化语言里至少保留了 97.07% 的父模型内部切分，cluster-internal cut 数量与父 tokenizer 相差不超过 1.54%。这说明现有 byteification 流程虽然去掉了显式 tokenizer 接口，但切分偏好几乎原样继承，cluster 内部碎裂并没有真正解决。论文据此论证：如果先删除 cluster-internal cuts，再训练边界预测器，监督会更干净，也更符合 byte-level 接口想要达到的语言无关性。17:T7be,The paper has two main technical components. The first is target construction. Instead of inheriting all parent tokenizer boundaries, the authors define grapheme-aware supervision in two forms: an every-cluster target that keeps every grapheme boundary, and a retained-parent target that keeps only those parent-tokenizer cuts already aligned with grapheme boundaries. Grapheme clusters are chosen because their boundaries are representable across encodings, stable under span-preserving edits, and directly isolate the continuation-vs-new-cluster distinction that encoding order can obscure.

The second component is the encoding comparison. The paper uses Universal Byte-Level Encoding (UBE), which keeps one- and two-byte UTF-8 encodings unchanged but rewrites longer scalars as UTF-16 little-endian bytes. For codepoints that would take three bytes in UTF-8, UBE shortens them to two symbols and, more importantly, exposes the low byte first. Within a known 256-codepoint page, that first symbol often identifies the codepoint directly. To separate stream-length effects from byte-order effects, the authors introduce UBE-BE, a big-endian control with the same routing and stream length as UBE but reversed byte order inside each UTF-16 code unit. This is a strong control: if UBE wins over both UTF-8 and UBE-BE, the gain cannot be explained by shorter streams alone.

They train small causal boundary predictors on matched FineWeb-2 text and evaluate on a multilingual FLORES-200 panel. Errors are split into scalar-end decisions and false cuts inside scalars; the latter can be removed by a rule-based mask without affecting scalar-end decisions. A particularly clean diagnostic is the constructed-pair test: pairs with identical left context, next scalars on the same 256-codepoint page, but opposite correct boundary decisions. On such pairs, failure is not about optimization difficulty. It is about whether the encoding exposes enough information at one-symbol lookahead.18:T6ed,Three results carry most of the paper. First, on the 17-language FLORES-200 panel for the every-cluster target with one-symbol lookahead, UTF-8 yields 8.76% balanced error at scalar ends, UBE drops this to 0.06%, while UBE-BE remains at 8.62%. This is the clearest evidence that byte order, not just shorter streams, drives the improvement. Second, on 17,204 constructed pairs with identical left context but opposite correct decisions, the trained UBE predictors solve all pairs correctly for every seed. UTF-8 and UBE-BE cannot, because both expose the same first symbol at the critical position. That turns the argument from empirical correlation into representational necessity.

Third, the paper examines Korean and Chinese, where evaluated grapheme clusters are single scalars, so the task becomes subword-boundary selection rather than grapheme continuation. Even there, UBE reduces total retained-parent errors by 72.91% and 35.29% relative to UTF-8 at one-symbol lookahead. Across eight additional scripts, reductions range from 67.32% to 99.55%. The paper also notes a useful nuance: when a script’s main Unicode block lies within a single 256-codepoint page, UBE-BE stays close to UTF-8, consistent with the mechanism that low-byte-first matters most when it reveals within-page identity early.

The audit of released byteification models is also important. For Bwen-8B, a Bolmo-style conversion of Qwen3-8B-Base, at least 97.07% of the parent model’s interior cuts are retained in each of 18 high-fragmentation languages, and the grapheme-internal cut count stays within 1.54% of the parent tokenizer. The key empirical pattern is that a small amount of agentic traces helps on top of natural data, but the stage should not become a long SFT substitute.1d:T585,The paper is organized around three ideas. First is hardware-model co-design. MI350X offers about 1.6x the HBM capacity of B200, and the authors do not treat migration as a same-model, same-batch portability exercise. Instead, they redesign the training setup to exploit the extra memory: larger per-GPU batch sizes, less activation checkpointing, rebalanced data/model parallelism, and efficient embedding re-sharding. Importantly, the extra HBM is also spent on model quality, such as longer inputs, larger hidden sizes, and larger embedding tables, not only on throughput. Second is the analytical performance model Origami. DLRM workloads involve fragmented GEMM shapes, where offline autotuning is expensive and often brittle. Origami predicts tile configurations directly, reportedly in microseconds, and reaches 93% accuracy relative to exhaustive autotuning. The paper emphasizes that the model extends to multi-chiplet architectures, which is particularly relevant for AMD hardware. Third is an agentic workflow for kernel optimization. The authors codify microarchitecture-aware tuning steps such as configuration selection, PID swizzling, occupancy hints, specialized instruction usage, and tree-reduction rewrites for atomic-heavy kernels. The key point is not the use of an agent by itself, but the conversion of expert-only kernel-porting knowledge into a structured and partially automated process.1e:T4a4,The experiments are mainly on Meta production DLRMs. End to end, MI350X reaches a geometric-mean throughput of 101% relative to the B200 baseline across a representative set of production models, indicating rough parity after substantial optimization. The hardware-model co-design changes deliver about a 20% training speedup together with more than 0.1% improvement in normalized entropy, showing that larger HBM can be converted into both efficiency and model-quality gains. Origami predicts near-optimal kernel configurations with 93% accuracy relative to exhaustive autotuning, while making decisions in microseconds. The agentic workflow yields roughly 1.6x to 2x speedups across handwritten and compiler-generated kernels, and the tree-reduction approach for atomic bottlenecks reaches up to 4x on custom kernels. The paper is also candid about remaining gaps: MI350X GEMM performance still lags in some cases because of emulated TF32 overhead and the lower maturity of hipBLAS versus cuBLAS on irregular matrix shapes. The authors mention successful LLM training optimization on clusters with more than 2,000 MI350X GPUs, but they do not provide detailed LLM-specific results here.1f:T87c,方法很朴素，但实现细节做得比较完整。作者观察到，对 ReLU 或 ReLU^2 前馈层，反向传播所需保存的信息并不是完整 dense activation，而是两部分：哪些位置为正，以及这些正值本身。零值不需要存，正值的符号位也恒为 0，因此对 BF16/FP8 来说还可以进一步省掉 sign bit。基于这个观察，BitSparse 用两部分表示激活：一个 bitmask 记录非零位置，一个紧凑 value buffer 顺序存储所有非零值的 payload。这样在 backward 需要恢复激活时，再根据 bitmask 把非零值 scatter 回原位置，重建出与原始缓存完全一致的张量。

实现上，论文强调它是 GPU-resident 的格式，而不是离线压缩。压缩和解压都写成 Triton kernel，并融合进 autograd function。为了避免 host synchronization，作者使用预分配的共享 value buffer，并让 offsets 保持在设备端管理。解码采用 tile-parallel reconstruction，以降低 backward 时的访存和调度开销。支持的数据类型包括 BF16 和 FP8；可选的 sign-bit packing 会把正值的冗余符号位去掉，使压缩率更接近理论极限。

论文还给了一个信息论分析。作者把每个激活位置建模为：以概率 rho 为零，否则携带一个均匀分布的 (d-1)-bit payload。于是每个位置的最优平均码长由 support entropy h2(rho) 加上非零值的 payload 成本组成。这个分析给出了实现格式的理论上限和 break-even sparsity threshold：只有当稀疏度足够高时，bitmask + compact values 才比 dense 存储更省。这个部分的价值在于，它说明 BitSparse 不是“任何 ReLU 网络都稳赚”，而是依赖实际训练中出现的高稀疏度。作者在 Nemotron-H 上测得约 92% 的前馈激活稀疏度，因此落在很有利的区间。

从训练系统角度看，BitSparse 与 checkpointing 的取舍也很清楚。checkpointing 用重算换显存，几乎不依赖激活分布；BitSparse 用编码/解码开销换显存，但不需要重跑前向，且是无损的。它更像是第三条路径：当激活天然稀疏时，直接压缩缓存本身。20:T859,The core observation is simple but useful. For a ReLU or ReLU^2 feed-forward block, the information needed for backward is not the full dense activation tensor. It is the support of positive entries and the positive values themselves. Zero entries need not be stored, and positive values have a redundant sign bit that can also be removed for BF16 and FP8 formats. BitSparse therefore stores activations as two components: a bitmask for nonzero locations and a compact value buffer containing only the nonzero payloads. During backward, the original activation tensor is reconstructed exactly by scattering those values back according to the bitmask.

The implementation is designed to stay entirely on the GPU. Compression and decompression are implemented as Triton kernels and fused into a custom autograd function. To avoid host synchronization, the system uses a preallocated shared value buffer with offsets managed on device. Reconstruction is tile-parallel to keep backward efficient. The format supports BF16 and FP8, and optional sign-bit packing pushes compression closer to the information-theoretic limit.

A nice part of the paper is the entropy analysis. Each activation entry is modeled as zero with probability rho, otherwise carrying a uniformly distributed (d-1)-bit payload. Under that model, the optimal average code length per entry is the support entropy h2(rho) plus the expected payload cost of nonzeros. This gives a clean reference point for the achievable compression ratio and the break-even sparsity threshold. That matters because the method is only attractive when sparsity is high enough; it is not a free win for every ReLU network. The authors report about 92% feed-forward activation sparsity in Nemotron-H, which places the method in a favorable regime.

Relative to activation checkpointing, the trade-off is also clear. Checkpointing saves memory by recomputing forward activations later. BitSparse saves memory by encoding the cache itself, with no recomputation and exact recovery, at the cost of codec overhead. It is a third option that becomes compelling when activations are naturally sparse.21:T488,The experiments cover compression ratio, codec throughput, standalone MLP workloads, and end-to-end language-model forward/backward workloads. Three numbers stand out. First, in MLP tests, BitSparse reduces peak allocated memory by up to 48%. Second, in language-model training settings, memory per token drops by about 31% for Modded-NanoGPT and about 30% for Nemotron-H. Third, the decode path reaches roughly 97% of attainable bandwidth, suggesting the implementation is close to the hardware limit rather than being dominated by software inefficiency.

The paper also evaluates BF16 and FP8 support and shows additional gains from sign-bit packing. Runtime overhead is reported to be small, and the recovered activations are exactly equal to the original cached activations, which cleanly separates this method from lossy activation compression.

The main caveat is scope. The gains rely on ReLU or ReLU^2 activations and high sparsity. The method does not directly apply to standard SwiGLU or GELU-based LLMs. The empirical study is therefore centered on sparse-activation models such as Nemotron-H and Modded-NanoGPT, not on generic Transformer training.22:T4a0,The method defines a three-action controller over trust, fallback, and expand. Trust emits the current evaluator-preferred answer, fallback emits a conservative answer that avoids further continuation, and expand buys one more unit of inference before the controller acts again. The same framework covers both width expansion and revision expansion.
For terminal actions, the target value is success probability minus compute cost. For expand, the ideal target is the Bellman continuation value. In practice, the system learns one confidence head per action: trust and fallback estimate terminal answer success, while expand estimates a rollout-based continuation-success surrogate. These predictions are then post-hoc calibrated, and an optional uncertainty penalty is applied near brittle decision boundaries. The theory gives two main results: local action selection is stable when score error is smaller than the compute-adjusted action gap, and regret accumulates along the realized expansion path. A notable design choice is that the expand head predicts a success-based surrogate rather than the full downstream-cost-aware Bellman value, which keeps the controller lightweight.23:T425,The setup fixes K language models. For each question q, model i induces an answer distribution p_i(a|q) over a finite answer set. An ensemble weight vector w defines a mixture distribution by convexly combining the model distributions; operationally, each generation can be assigned to a model sampled according to w. The target is clean risk: over the population of questions, the gold answer must be the unique mode of the infinite-generation mixture distribution. Since the p_i are unknown, the learner observes N sampled answers from each model on each of Q labeled questions. A zero-buffer ERM can overfit finite-N noise: an empirical margin may be positive even when the true clean margin is non-positive. The proposed buffered ERM counts a question as solved only when the empirical margin exceeds a positive threshold epsilon. Under a margin condition with exponent beta and fixed numbers of models and answers, a calibrated buffer yields excess clean risk of order Q^{-1/2} + N^{-beta/2}, up to logarithmic factors, with a matching minimax lower bound.24:Tc20,作者提出的 LangDiT 可以理解为一个面向 CDLM 的专用 Transformer denoiser，核心设计围绕三件事展开：噪声状态如何进 backbone、离散词表预测如何和连续表示接口、以及 self-conditioning 该以多强的方式介入训练。

第一部分是 backbone 内部的归一化与噪声调制。LangDiT 在特征路径上使用 backbone RMSNorm，在注意力里额外使用 query-key RMSNorm。前者控制隐藏状态尺度，后者直接控制 attention logit 的尺度稳定性。这个选择很像把 LLM 里对训练稳定性的经验，和 diffusion 模型里对噪声条件敏感的需求结合起来。作者的隐含判断是：CDLM 的输入分布随噪声水平变化更剧烈，若 attention logit 尺度不稳，去噪网络更容易在不同 γ 下出现优化困难。除此之外，他们还把 noise conditioning 做得更“宽”，也就是给噪声条件更大的调制容量，而不是只做一个很窄的时间步嵌入后轻量注入。原因是语言去噪里不同噪声区间对应的任务差异很大：高噪声时更像全局猜测，低噪声时更像局部校正，网络需要更强的条件化能力。

第二部分是 likelihood shortcut 的梯度路由与校准。LangFlow / Plaid 这类连续语言模型通常会通过 codebook 或 embedding matrix，把连续状态和离散词表联系起来。LangDiT 保留了这种 likelihood shortcut，但不让 shortcut 的 embedding matrix 直接承受全部梯度，而是对其做 detach，避免训练过度依赖这条捷径，导致 token embedding 学成“为 shortcut 服务”的几何结构，而不是为 denoising backbone 服务。作者还对 shortcut 做了 gated 设计和 calibration，意思是 shortcut 不是无条件强加到 logits 上，而是根据置信度或训练状态控制其影响强度。这个点很关键，因为在 CDLM 里 shortcut 往往既有帮助也有风险：它能更快把连续状态映射回词表，但也可能让模型绕过真正的上下文建模，形成脆弱的局部匹配。

第三部分是 confidence-gated training self-conditioning。Self-conditioning 在 diffusion 模型里常见，但直接把上一步预测强行喂回去，容易在训练早期引入错误累积，尤其语言离散空间里错误 token 分布会很尖。作者不是简单地开或关 self-conditioning，而是按模型当前预测置信度做门控，只在更可信的时候让先前预测更强地影响当前去噪。这个设计背后的逻辑是：self-conditioning 的收益来自跨步一致性，但前提是前一步信息足够可靠；否则它会把噪声放大成偏置。

整篇论文的方法学上最好的地方，是作者尽量把变量控制住。他们先在 LangFlow 框架里做七阶段 cumulative ablation，每次只加一类设计，保持表示、目标函数、噪声日程和采样器不变。之后再把兼容的设计迁移到 Plaid-style CDLM，测试可复用性。这样读者能更清楚地看到“架构”本身带来的增益，而不是把训练预算、采样步数、目标函数变化混在一起。25:T828,实验主要在 OpenWebText 无条件生成上做，序列长度 1,024。最核心的是 matched comparison：在相同训练设置、相同采样预算 128 NFE 下，作者用一个七阶段 LangFlow ladder 逐步叠加架构改动，GenPPL 从 64.26 降到 53.66。这个幅度不小，说明单靠 backbone 设计就能显著改善连续语言生成质量。与此同时，mean per-sample unigram entropy 从 5.416 变到 5.391，变化不大，说明提升不只是靠把输出分布简单收缩成更低熵文本；至少在这组对比里，质量提升不是明显依赖退化式 mode collapse。

作者还报告了更长训练下的结果：一个 660k 的 LangFlow checkpoint 和一个 520k 的 Plaid checkpoint，来自 1M update 计划，在更大 sampling budget 下分别达到 GenPPL 21.72 和 11.33。论文也很谨慎地说明，这些 extended-training 分数不能直接归因于架构，因为训练步数和采样预算都变了。这种区分是对的，读的时候也要把“matched ablation”与“best achieved score”分开看。

从消融角度，最值得关注的是六类 denoiser-design intervention 的累积效果。虽然题面摘要没有逐项给出全部数字，但全文主线很清楚：backbone normalization、query-key normalization、wider noise conditioning、likelihood-shortcut gradient routing、shortcut calibration、以及 confidence-gated self-conditioning 都各自贡献了一部分，叠加后形成稳定收益。若正文或附录给出了每一步对 GenPPL、entropy、sampling cost 的影响，建议逐项核对，因为这能帮助判断哪些改动是“普适稳定性增强”，哪些更依赖具体 formulation。

另一个实验价值在于 transfer。作者没有停留在 LangFlow 自家设定，而是把兼容组件迁到 Plaid-style CDLM，并保留 Plaid 原生 prediction interface。这个设计说明他们不是想用新架构重写整个方法，而是测试这些架构原则能否跨连续语言建模变体成立。对后续研究者来说，这比单一框架里的最优数字更有参考意义。26:Tb8f,LangDiT is a Transformer denoiser tailored for CDLMs, and its design is organized around three interfaces: how noisy continuous states enter the backbone, how the model connects continuous states to discrete vocabulary prediction, and how self-conditioning should be used during training.

The first set of changes concerns normalization and noise conditioning inside the backbone. LangDiT uses backbone RMSNorm for hidden-state scale control and query-key RMSNorm for direct control of attention-logit scale. This is a sensible adaptation to CDLMs, where the input distribution changes substantially across noise levels. If attention logits drift in scale as noise varies, optimization becomes harder and denoising quality degrades. The model also uses wider noise conditioning, giving the noise signal more capacity to modulate computation. That choice reflects a real property of language diffusion: high-noise denoising behaves more like global hypothesis formation, while low-noise denoising behaves more like local correction, so the network benefits from stronger conditional modulation.

The second set of changes concerns the likelihood shortcut. In LangFlow- and Plaid-style models, a shortcut path often maps continuous states to vocabulary logits through the codebook or embedding matrix. LangDiT keeps this shortcut but changes how gradients flow through it. The embedding matrix on the shortcut path is detached, which prevents the model from overfitting the embedding geometry to the shortcut itself. Without this, the shortcut can become an overly dominant path that weakens the burden on the contextual denoiser. The shortcut is also gated and calibrated rather than added in an unconditional way. This is important because the shortcut is useful but dangerous: it can accelerate token recovery, but it can also encourage brittle local matching instead of robust contextual denoising.

The third component is confidence-gated training self-conditioning. Self-conditioning is common in diffusion models, but naively feeding previous predictions back into the model can be harmful in language, especially early in training when token predictions are unreliable and errors are sharp in the discrete space. LangDiT therefore gates self-conditioning by confidence, allowing previous predictions to influence the current denoising step more strongly only when they are trustworthy enough. The intuition is simple: self-conditioning helps when it stabilizes cross-step consistency, but hurts when it amplifies noisy guesses.

Methodologically, one of the strongest aspects of the paper is variable control. The authors first run a seven-stage cumulative ablation within LangFlow while keeping the representation, objective, noise schedule, and sampler fixed. Only then do they transfer compatible components to a Plaid-style CDLM. That makes it much easier to attribute gains to architecture rather than to changes in training budget or formulation.27:T6d4,The main experiments are on unconditional OpenWebText generation at sequence length 1,024. The most important result is the matched architectural comparison: under the same training setup and the same sampling budget of 128 NFE, the seven-stage LangFlow ladder reduces GenPPL from 64.26 to 53.66. That is a substantial improvement coming from architecture alone. At the same time, mean per-sample unigram entropy changes only slightly, from 5.416 to 5.391, which suggests that the gain is not simply due to collapsing the output distribution into lower-entropy text.

The paper also reports longer-training results: a 660k LangFlow checkpoint and a 520k Plaid checkpoint, from 1M-update plans, reach GenPPL 21.72 and 11.33 respectively at larger sampling budgets. Importantly, the authors explicitly note that these numbers should not be interpreted as architecture-only gains, because both training budget and sampling budget differ. That distinction is correct and worth preserving when reading the paper.

The ablation structure is one of the main strengths. The paper studies six denoiser-design interventions and shows their cumulative effect: backbone normalization, query-key normalization, wider noise conditioning, likelihood-shortcut gradient routing, shortcut calibration, and confidence-gated self-conditioning. Even without every intermediate number in the prompt, the narrative is clear: each component contributes part of the gain, and together they produce a more effective denoiser. Another useful aspect is transfer. The authors do not stop at LangFlow; they reuse compatible components in a Plaid-style CDLM while keeping Plaid’s native prediction interface. That makes the architectural claims more credible and more reusable.28:T525,Read it in the order of problem framing, architecture, controlled ablation, and transfer. Start with the introduction to understand why default choices from causal LLMs and image DiTs are not obviously appropriate for CDLMs. Then go straight to Table 1 and Figure 3, which explain the LangDiT data flow: noisy embeddings, optional self-conditioning, bidirectional Transformer, untied vocabulary head, gated likelihood shortcut, and clean-state estimate. That figure is the structural core of the paper.

Next, focus on the seven-stage cumulative ablation and the main result figures. Keep two kinds of evidence separate: matched-setting architecture-only improvements versus best numbers obtained under longer training and larger sampling budgets. Then inspect three technical details carefully: why both backbone RMSNorm and query-key RMSNorm are needed, why the likelihood shortcut uses detach plus calibration, and why self-conditioning is confidence-gated rather than always on.

If you only have about an hour, prioritize the introduction, the architecture overview, the main ablation figures/tables, and the Plaid transfer section. If you plan to work on diffusion LMs directly, the implementation and training details in the appendix are likely worth careful study because they will matter for reproducibility.29:T504,TIPS formulates finite-step dLLM decoding as a finite-horizon Markov decision process. At each step, the frozen dLLM proposes token distributions for masked positions. A lightweight controller then outputs a binary next-step visibility action for every response position. For a masked position, visibility means committing the current proposal; non-visibility leaves it masked. For an already visible position, visibility keeps the token; non-visibility remasks it so that it can be regenerated later. This single action space covers both unmasking and revision. The controller is a shallow two-layer transformer using visibility-aware confidence features, mask indicators, and normalized decoding time. A key design choice is to decouple ordering from pace. The policy ranks positions by relative preference, while a fixed power-law schedule determines the expected visible fraction. A shared shift on the policy logits matches that target fraction without changing the relative preferences. Training has two stages: supervised warmup from reference-derived visibility decisions, followed by group-relative policy optimization using terminal answer correctness. Only the auxiliary controller is updated; no gradients through the dLLM and no backbone sequence likelihood are required.2a:T708,The paper first develops the exploration-dilemma argument. In a shared-expert MoE layer, every token always receives the shared-expert contribution, while only a subset of routed experts is selected conditionally. During pretraining, the shared branch tends to dominate the learned token representation because it captures common knowledge for all tokens. Once that happens, changing the routed experts often produces only limited variation in the final features. Alternative routes become harder to distinguish, so the router receives weaker signals for meaningful exploration.

At the same time, fine-grained expert segmentation increases both E and K, which explodes the number of possible expert subsets. The paper gives a concrete example: moving from (E, K) = (8, 1) to (64, 8) increases the routing space from 8 possibilities to about 4.4 × 10^9 combinations. So the architecture demands more strategic exploration exactly when shared experts make exploration less effective.

MirrorMoE is proposed to resolve this mismatch by adaptively shrinking the routed-expert exploration space on a per-token basis. The method is derived by mirroring routing logits through sign negation. The intuition is not to add more randomness, but to suppress routed experts adaptively so that the effective search space better matches the model’s exploration capability under shared-expert dominance. This is different from simply reducing K globally, injecting noise, or tweaking load-balancing losses. The paper frames MirrorMoE as a way to improve trainability and route discoverability, not as a way to increase theoretical expressiveness. It also claims a theoretical characterization of the adaptivity, suggesting the suppression behavior is tied to routing structure rather than being a heuristic knob.2b:T76c,The experiments are built around a clear question: when does adding shared experts help, and when does it interfere with the benefits of larger K? The authors train matched MoEs with and without shared experts at four scales, from 100M to 2.4B total parameters. At each scale, they fix the total number of experts E and vary the number of activated experts K over {6, 8, 10}. This is a good stress test because larger K simultaneously increases expressiveness and enlarges the routing search space.

Three results stand out. First, the benefit of shared experts diminishes as K increases. In some settings, shared-expert MoEs even get worse when K becomes larger. That is the empirical signature of the exploration dilemma: more combinatorial capacity does not translate into better pretraining because the model cannot explore the larger routing space effectively. Second, MirrorMoE consistently improves this regime. The clearest numbers given in the provided content are on the 2.4B model: +0.67 points in pretraining performance and +1.64 points on downstream performance. Third, MirrorMoE restores the expected gains from increasing K and allows shared-expert MoEs to consistently outperform their non-shared counterparts again. That is important because it suggests the issue is not shared experts per se, but the training mismatch created when shared experts are combined with a large routing space.

The excerpt does not include all ablations, but the introduction already indicates the key comparisons: shared vs non-shared, different K values, and with vs without MirrorMoE across multiple scales. 算法上，第一步是把 residual learning 明确成 on-policy rollout。训练时不再依赖离线预生成的 residual states，而是用当前模型在线生成 denoising trajectory：每一步模型接收当前 partially denoised block 以及上一步 residual context，输出新的 token 分布和新的 residual，再继续 rollout。这样训练看到的状态与推理时一致，避免 exposure mismatch。论文强调，若用离线 residual 监督，模型学到的是“如何利用别的策略生成的 residual”，而不是“如何利用自己会生成的 residual”。

第二步是稳定化 residual pathway。作者观察到在共享优化器下，residual 分支比 backbone 更容易快速漂移，导致训练不稳。ORL 因此对 residual pathway 做了 rescaling，使其更新节奏与 backbone 更接近；同时引入基于 rollout entropy 的 supervision gating：当某些位置已经足够 confident，就不再继续强行 sharpen，避免过度收缩导致错误被放大。这里的设计不是简单 regularization，而是在控制“哪些状态值得继续 refinement”。

第三步是提出 adjacent entropy-contraction objective。仅用最终 token 监督，模型知道每一步应该朝最终答案靠近，但不知道每一步应该推进多少。作者发现很多基线在 denoising steps 上 entropy 几乎不下降，因此虽然最终能收敛到正确 token，单步信息增益却很小，TPF 提升有限。ORL 直接要求相邻步骤之间的预测分布熵收缩，也就是后一步要比前一步更确定，但这种收缩又受前述 entropy gating 约束，避免在已经低熵的位置继续盲目压缩。这个目标抓住了 DLM 的核心：每次前向不仅要“更对”，还要“更敢提交”。

系统上，ORL 不是把 on-policy 训练当成概念验证，而是实现了可扩展的 trajectory pipeline。论文描述了异步捕获 residual states、根据显存压力决定保留还是 offload、把不规则长度和不同阶段的轨迹状态打包成稠密 batch，以及用 compute-aware scheduler 平衡 GPU 上 rollout 与训练的负载。文中还提到专门的 staircase attention/packing 设计，用来处理逐步解 mask 带来的非规则计算图。这部分很重要，因为没有这些工程设计，exact on-policy residual learning 很难在大模型上跑起来。2e:T87a,论文的实验重点围绕三个问题展开：on-policy 是否必要、entropy-contraction 是否真的提升 refinement speed、以及系统实现是否能把这种训练跑到足够大规模。

从定性现象看，作者先展示了 residual predictions 在中间步骤经常已经提前包含最终 token 的强信号，这说明 residual context 不是噪声缓存，而是可学习的计算再利用通道。随后他们给出一个关键负面观察：如果只做常规中间态监督，denoising 过程中 entropy 基本持平，tokens-per-forward 几乎不增长。这直接支持了“最终正确率监督不足以优化并行推进速度”的论点。

主实验里，ORL 相比离线 residual 学习、无 on-policy rollout 的变体、以及不带 entropy-contraction 的版本，都能得到更好的 speed–quality Pareto。摘要中提到 DiffusionGemma 一类 residual DLM 已可达到 20+ TPF、单卡 H100 约 1230 tok/s；ORL 的贡献不是单纯刷新一个吞吐数字，而是在相近或更高质量下，把 residual context 真正训练成能持续收缩不确定性的机制。全文强调的指标包括不同 forward budget 下的质量曲线、平均 TPF、各 denoising step 的 entropy 变化，以及 rollout 训练稳定性。消融显示：去掉 on-policy 训练后，推理时 residual 轨迹分布偏移，质量和 TPF 都下降；去掉 residual rescaling，训练更容易震荡；去掉 entropy gating，会出现过度 sharpen；去掉 adjacent entropy-contraction，则中间步骤的熵下降幅度明显变小，说明模型没有学会更激进但可控的 refinement。

系统实验则证明 exact on-policy residual learning 不是只能在小规模玩具设置上成立。作者展示了异步轨迹采集、状态搬运和 batch packing 后，训练吞吐与资源利用率可以维持在可接受范围，说明这种训练范式具备继续放大到更大 DLM 的工程可行性。由于给出的全文片段没有完整数表，这里不硬填具体增益数字；但从文中叙述看，提升是沿 speed–quality frontier 展开的，而不是只在单一质量点或单一步数预算上偶然有效。2f:T551,This is a must-read for researchers interested in non-autoregressive language modeling. Its contribution is not just another diffusion decoding heuristic. It reframes residual context as a training paradigm: the learning distribution must follow the model's own rollout states, and the objective must explicitly reward uncertainty reduction across steps rather than assuming final-token supervision will automatically produce faster refinement. That matters because DLMs differ from AR LMs in a fundamental way. They are not only learning what token should appear, but also how much progress should be made per forward pass. If that second part is left implicit, a model may reach decent final quality while making very little information gain per step, which defeats the point of parallel generation.

From a pretraining perspective, the paper is valuable for three reasons. First, it extends on-policy learning beyond RL or post-training into the generative modeling objective itself. Second, it introduces entropy contraction as a direct proxy for refinement speed, which is closer to the real optimization target of parallel decoding than plain token-level supervision. Third, it treats trajectory-dependent training as a joint algorithm-systems problem, which is likely necessary for any serious scaling attempt in diffusion or any-order language modeling.30:T9a0,ORL has two tightly coupled components: an on-policy learning algorithm and a trajectory-aware training system.

On the algorithmic side, the first move is to train on exact model-generated residual trajectories. Instead of relying on offline residual states, ORL rolls out the current model online. At each denoising step, the model takes the current partially denoised block together with the residual context from the previous step, produces a new predictive distribution and a new residual state, and continues the rollout. This aligns the training distribution with the inference distribution. The key claim is that learning to consume someone else's residuals is not the same as learning to consume your own.

The second ingredient is stabilization of the residual pathway. The authors observe that under a shared optimizer, the residual branch can drift much faster than the backbone. ORL therefore rescales the residual pathway so that its effective update pace better matches the backbone. It also applies entropy-based supervision gating: positions that are already sufficiently confident are not pushed to sharpen further. This prevents over-contraction and reduces the risk of amplifying early mistakes.

The third ingredient is the adjacent entropy-contraction objective. Final-token supervision tells the model where each intermediate state should end up, but not how much progress each step should make. The paper shows that under standard supervision, entropy often stays nearly flat across denoising steps, and tokens-per-forward barely improves. ORL explicitly encourages the predictive distribution at step t+1 to be lower-entropy than at step t, subject to the gating mechanism above. This directly optimizes refinement speed: each forward pass should not only be more correct, but also more decisive.

On the systems side, ORL implements exact on-policy residual learning at scale. It asynchronously captures residual states off the decoding critical path, uses memory-adaptive transport to decide whether states stay resident or are offloaded, packs irregular trajectory states into dense training batches, and uses a compute-aware scheduler to balance rollout and training workloads across GPUs. The paper also mentions specialized staircase-style attention and packing to handle the irregular structure induced by progressive unmasking. These details are not peripheral; they are what make the training recipe practical beyond toy settings.31:T9ba,The experiments are organized around three questions: whether on-policy learning is necessary, whether entropy contraction improves refinement speed, and whether the resulting training pipeline is scalable.

The paper first provides a useful qualitative observation: intermediate residual predictions often already contain strong signals of the final tokens before commitment. That supports the idea that residual context is a meaningful computational state rather than a noisy byproduct. It then presents a key negative result: with ordinary intermediate supervision alone, entropy remains almost flat across denoising steps and tokens-per-forward barely increases. This is one of the most important empirical findings in the paper, because it shows that final correctness does not automatically translate into faster parallel refinement.

In the main comparisons, ORL improves the speed–quality Pareto over offline residual learning, non-on-policy variants, and versions without entropy contraction. The abstract situates the work in the context of residual DLMs such as DiffusionGemma, which already reaches 20+ tokens per forward and around 1,230 tok/s on one H100. ORL's contribution is not merely a single throughput number; it is that residual context becomes a learned mechanism for sustained uncertainty reduction across steps while preserving or improving quality. The paper emphasizes metrics such as quality under different forward budgets, average tokens per forward, entropy trajectories across denoising steps, and training stability.

The ablations are especially informative. Removing on-policy rollout leads to a train-test mismatch in residual trajectories and hurts both quality and TPF. Removing residual rescaling makes optimization less stable. Removing entropy gating causes over-sharpening. Removing the adjacent entropy-contraction loss substantially weakens entropy reduction across steps, showing that the model does not naturally learn aggressive but controlled refinement from final supervision alone.

The systems experiments show that exact on-policy residual learning can be run with acceptable throughput and utilization once asynchronous trajectory capture, state transport, and dense packing are in place. The provided excerpt does not include the full numeric tables, so it is better not to invent exact gains here. What is clear from the text is that the improvement is along the speed–quality frontier rather than a narrow win at one fixed budget.32:T5f3,Read this one in full. If the upcoming bytes can be copied from recent context, they are old information; if they cannot, new information is entering the stream, and that is where a patch should start. Formally, for each position t, m_t is the length of the longest prefix of the future byte stream that appears within the previous 128 bytes, capped at 16. Novelty is defined as -m_t, so shorter matches mean higher novelty. Since m_t depends on future bytes, it cannot be used directly online. The authors therefore build a causal approximation: a lookup table indexed by the previous two bytes, storing the average value of -m_t observed under that context. The table is fit on 4 MB of raw text in seconds on CPU, with backoff to one-byte context and then the global mean for rare contexts. At inference time, patching is just a table lookup plus thresholding to hit a target patch rate.

Several design choices are notable. The method needs no labels, no reference model, and no loss-based ablation signal, making it cheaper than both entropy patching and the earlier dependence-table approach. It changes the routing principle from surprisal-seeking to novelty-seeking. The paper also evaluates two variants: nov, fit on GSM8K and MATH training solutions, and novc, fit on a raw pretraining-corpus sample, to test whether the effect depends on math-specific fitting. Baselines include BLT’s entropy threshold, the prior dependence table, and a hand-written syntax+entropy rule. Models are BLT-style systems trained from scratch with cross-attention pooling, a windowed local decoder, and 128-byte context, at 1M, 12M, and 50M parameters on a 1.9 GB math-heavy corpus, with matched patch rates around 11% and three seeds per setup.35:T79b,The main gains appear only once the model is large enough to use the extra global compute effectively. At 1M parameters, all methods are near the floor on computed results, around 3–5%, and only the hand-written syntax rule noticeably improves final answers. At 12M, novelty patching separates clearly: final-answer accuracy reaches 71.5%, versus 46.6% for entropy and 56.7% for dependence; computed-result accuracy rises from 5.8% under entropy to 10.1%. At 50M, the gap becomes large: computed results reach 57.5%, compared with 20.7% for entropy and 35.1% for dependence; final answers reach 89.5%, compared with 59.9% and 78.2%. Entropy also shows high seed variance on computed results, suggesting that it is not just weak but unstable for this failure mode. The paper checks that gradient clipping at 50M is neutral for the entropy baseline, so the result is not an artifact of training stabilization.

Generalization results are mixed in an informative way. The corpus-fitted novelty table, built from raw pretraining text rather than math-solution data, preserves the main gain, which means the signal is not purely task-specific. Outside math, novelty lowers bits per byte on prose, but only ties entropy on source code and synthetic execution traces, both in bpb and exact token accuracy. The mechanism analysis explains why: computed results often have ordinary surprisal, so entropy misses them, while novelty tends to spike where a new result string begins in math solutions. In code and traces, important structure does not align as cleanly with “new literal starts here,” so the advantage disappears. The discussion of boundary enrichment is also useful: the metric optimized by learned chunkers such as SOMBRERO is actually highest for entropy, even though entropy is worst on computed results. That is a strong warning that local chunking metrics can be misaligned with the positions that matter for reasoning-like behavior.36:T4bd,Read the introduction first to understand the target claim: high entropy is not the same as high value for global compute. A quick pass takes 20–30 minutes; a deeper read should focus on the novelty-table construction, threshold matching, the baseline design, and the mechanism analysis sections.37:T9a3,方法的出发点来自 Anari et al. (2026) 的精确 rejection correction。设 proposal 是把一个 block 内多个 token 按各自条件边缘独立采样得到的分布，target 是该 block 的真实联合条件分布。两者的 likelihood ratio 的对数，可以沿 block 内某个顺序分解成若干 token-level increment 之和；每个 increment 都能通过额外查询 score function 得到。问题在于完整求和要对 block 中每个 token 都查询一次。

SIRS 的关键改动，是不再显式求完整 log acceptance ratio，而是随机抽取一个 increment 来构造其无偏估计。单次估计只需一次查询，因此单个增量的获取成本与 block 大小脱钩。难点在于 rejection sampling 需要的是 acceptance probability，也就是 exp(log-ratio)；对 log-ratio 的无偏估计直接指数化后并不是 acceptance probability 的无偏估计。为此，论文引入 Poissonized Bernoulli factory：先采样一个 Poisson 个数的 clipped increments，再通过 Chen et al. (2026) 的 Bernoulli factory 机制，把这些随机增量组合成一个 [0,1] 内的随机接受概率，其期望恰好等于目标接受率。这样 rejection sampler 的边际输出仍可对准目标分布。

为了保证 Bernoulli factory 的输入可控，作者对 increment 做了区间 [-B, B] clipping。clipping 是 score 精确时唯一的近似来源。B 越大，理论误差越小，但期望查询次数会上升，文中给出每个 unmasking step 的期望查询成本上界为 (1+2B)e^{2B}，与 block size 无关。另一个重要技巧是 Rao-Blackwellization：虽然一次 score 查询是为某个随机选中的 increment 服务，但该查询实际上会返回当前剩余所有 masked 位置的条件分布，因此可以对所有可能的 token-level increment 做条件平均，降低方差而不增加查询成本。理论部分也证明了 Rao-Blackwellized increment 对 clipping-induced error 的上界更紧。

误差分析上，论文把输出分布与数据分布之间的 KL 分解为三部分：proposal 误差、acceptance probability 误差、clipping 误差。若 score function 精确，前两项消失，只剩 clipping 误差。并行独立采样对应 B=0，此时误差就是 block joint 与 marginals product 之间的完整相关性误差；SIRS 则只保留超出 clipping 区间的那部分增量贡献，因此当所有 increment 都落在 [-B,B] 内时可以恢复精确修正。38:T9c6,The starting point is the exact rejection correction of Anari et al. (2026). Let the proposal be the product of token-wise conditional marginals used by parallel sampling, and let the target be the true joint conditional distribution over the block. The log likelihood ratio between target and proposal can be decomposed into a sum of token-level increments along an ordering of the block, and each increment can be obtained from the score function. The problem is that evaluating the full sum requires one score query per token.

SIRS replaces the full evaluation with a single randomly sampled increment, yielding an unbiased estimator of the log acceptance ratio at the cost of one query. The main obstacle is that rejection sampling needs the acceptance probability, namely the exponential of that log ratio, and exponentiating an unbiased estimator does not preserve unbiasedness. To handle this, the paper uses a Poissonized Bernoulli factory following Chen et al. (2026): it samples a Poisson number of clipped increments and combines them into a random acceptance probability in [0,1] whose expectation matches the desired acceptance rate. Since rejection sampling only depends on the expected acceptance probability, the marginal output distribution remains correct under the construction.

To make the Bernoulli factory valid and stable, increments are clipped to [-B, B]. With an exact score model, clipping is the only source of approximation. Larger B reduces approximation error but increases query cost; the paper gives an expected per-step query bound of (1+2B)e^{2B}, independent of block size. A practically important refinement is Rao-Blackwellization. One score query returns conditionals for all remaining masked positions, so the sampled increment can be averaged over all eligible token choices at no extra query cost, reducing variance. The theory also shows a tighter clipping-error bound for the Rao-Blackwellized version.

The analysis decomposes the KL divergence between the sampler output and the data distribution into proposal error, acceptance-probability error, and clipping error. When the score function is exact, the first two vanish. Standard parallel sampling is recovered at B=0, where the method keeps the full correlation error between the block joint and the product of marginals. SIRS removes part of that error, leaving only the contribution from increments that exceed the clipping range; if all increments lie within [-B, B], the correction becomes exact.39:T4ad,The experimental section is intentionally narrow and theory-driven. The authors evaluate on two discrete systems with exact score functions, an Ising chain and a Pólya urn, where the KL divergence can be computed directly. This isolates the sampling error from model error.

Three findings matter. First, under the same score-query budget, SIRS with the Rao-Blackwellized increment achieves lower KL divergence than standard parallel sampling when within-block dependence is weak. Second, when dependence is strong, SIRS still corrects part of the bias, but the extra rejection and clipping overhead can make it less attractive than simply using smaller parallel blocks; the paper is explicit that small-block parallel sampling may remain cheaper in that regime. Third, Rao-Blackwellization consistently improves the estimator with essentially no extra query cost.

What is missing is also important: there are no large-scale language-model experiments, no end-to-end text generation quality results, and no wall-clock study on realistic MDLM or LLaDA-style systems. So the evidence is strongest on theoretical validity and controlled mechanism tests, not yet on practical large-model deployment.3a:T641,The model is a dual-view, dual-tower TSLM. The two views are chosen to preserve different aspects of the same signal. One view is a standard line plot, which retains absolute amplitudes, axis ranges, and the observed coordinate frame. This is the view needed for questions grounded in actual measurements. The second view is a normalized delay embedding. Delay embeddings reconstruct a time series as a trajectory in phase space using time-lagged observations, making temporal geometry more explicit. By normalizing this representation before rendering it, the model factors out positive amplitude rescaling and offsets while preserving temporal structure.

Architecturally, the line plot is processed by Qwen3-VL’s native vision encoder initialized from SigLIP-2, while the delay embedding is processed by a separate DINOv3 encoder. This is an important design choice: the authors do not simply concatenate the two images and feed them through a shared visual tower. They allow each view to develop a specialized visual representation before fusion. The resulting features are compressed into a compact token set—230 tokens for the line plot and 64 for the delay embedding—and then concatenated as input to a shared language model. In addition, the model uses DeepStack to inject multi-level visual features into early language-model layers, so the complementary views can interact with language processing beyond a single input projection. The method is therefore less about adding another tower and more about pairing distinct invariance profiles with dedicated encoders and sustained fusion.3b:T514,The model is built on Qwen3-VL-8B and evaluated on TSRBench, TSExam, and ChatTS. The headline result is 53.2% overall accuracy on TSRBench, compared with 36.7% for the strongest dedicated TSLM baseline reported in the paper, and close to GPT-5 with text-plus-visual input at 55.6%. The more informative comparison is the controlled ablation: under the same training setup, a plot-only variant reaches 45.2%, while adding the delay-embedding view raises performance to 53.2%, an 8.0-point gain. The gains are concentrated in reasoning, prediction, and decision-making, while perception changes little. That pattern supports the paper’s claim that complementary views help higher-level temporal reasoning rather than basic visual extraction.

The invariance experiments are also important. Under positive rescaling and offset shifts, the delay-only model remains nearly unchanged, showing that the normalized delay embedding indeed induces robustness to those transformations. The plot-only model is much more sensitive, which is expected because it preserves the original measurement frame. For a reader interested in modeling rather than benchmark chasing, these intervention results are more valuable than the raw leaderboard numbers because they tie performance back to representation properties.3c:T6a9,The design has a single-GPU part and a distributed part. On a single GPU, FlashMask-3 builds on the column-wise sparse representation from FlashMask. The mask is indexed by key position, while each key stores query-axis intervals through four boundary vectors, commonly denoted LTS, LTE, UTS, and UTE for lower- and upper-triangular regions. This avoids constructing an n by n mask and gives the kernel a compact representation of valid query-key tiles. The new kernel integrates this representation into FlashAttention-3’s Hopper execution model. It uses three-role warp specialization: a KV Index Generator scans the boundary vectors and produces the relevant tile or KV indices, a KV Loader issues asynchronous TMA loads, and MMA Consumers run WGMMA compute. Mask handling is moved out of the main compute loop into a producer-like stage, which reduces branch overhead and keeps the asynchronous pipeline full. A preemptive persistent-tile scheduler is added to reduce SM-level imbalance under irregular sparse masks. For distributed context parallelism, the key observation is that the mask is keyed by K positions but stores Q-axis intervals. Under any multi-chunk CP assignment, a rank-local mask can be obtained by elementwise clipping, shifting, and max operations over the boundary vectors. No cross-rank mask exchange is needed, and the resulting local representation can be passed to the same kernel. The distributed system then adds a sparsity-aware hierarchical load balancer, HCC-IPO, topology-aware hierarchical routing for forward all-gather, mask-driven communication pruning, and a backward reduce-scatter path overlapped with attention recomputation using bitmask-AMO synchronization.3d:T4ca,The evaluation covers microbenchmarks, context-parallel scaling, and end-to-end training. On a single H100, across 12 structured masks and sequence lengths from 4K to 128K, FlashMask-3 improves achieved TFLOPs over FlashMask by 45% to 141%, over FlexAttention by 34% to 71%, and over MagiAttention by 2% to 44%. These gains indicate that the improvement is not only from compact mask representation, but also from aligning mask-aware scheduling with Hopper’s TMA/WGMMA pipeline. In distributed context-parallel experiments with CP degrees from 4 to 32 and 8K tokens per device, it reaches 31% to 75% compute-communication overlap efficiency. Throughput improves by 1.80× to 3.71× over Megatron-Core CP ring, by 1.71× to 2.92× over Megatron-Core CP all-gather, and by 1.09× to 1.46× over MagiAttention. The end-to-end result is the most relevant for pretraining: on a 118B-A14B MoE model with 128K context over 128 H100 GPUs and CP degree 16, replacing Dual Chunk balancing and all-gather communication with the FlashMask-3 distributed extension raises training throughput by 7.3% to 11.0%. The smaller end-to-end gain is expected because the full step also includes MoE, MLP, other collectives, and scheduler overhead.3e:T42e,Read the mask-localization theorem first. The important idea is why a key-indexed representation that stores query intervals can be localized through clip-shift-max operations under arbitrary multi-chunk CP placement. Then read the Hopper kernel section and compare it with FA3 and the original FlashMask: the key implementation idea is the separation of mask scanning into a KV Index Generator role rather than embedding mask branches in the compute loop. The distributed sections on HCC-IPO, communication pruning, and recomputation-overlap are also worth careful reading, because long-context training often fails to scale due to imbalance and communication rather than raw MMA throughput. In the experiments, focus on the 12-mask single-GPU curves, CP-degree scaling, overlap-efficiency numbers, and the 118B-A14B MoE training table. Two questions are worth keeping in mind: which real pretraining masks cannot be expressed by the four-boundary representation, and whether dynamic multimodal packing could make mask construction or scheduling overhead visible again.3f:Ta7b,方法核心是 Virtual Head Attention。出发点很直接：如果把物理 query heads 数量减半，再把 KV heads 压到 2，理论上可以同时降低 attention 计算和 KV cache；问题在于这样会损失 head diversity。VHA 的做法不是恢复真实的更多 KV heads，而是在 query 侧“造出”虚拟头的差异，并在输出侧补跨组信息交互。

第一部分是 Q Premix。设原始 query heads 为 Hq，压缩后物理 query heads 变成 Hq'，通常是原来的一半；KV heads 固定为 2，因此每个 KV group 会对应更多 query heads。Premix 在每个 KV group 内对 query 做一个接近恒等映射的线性变换，把较少的物理 query heads 扩展成更多“虚拟 query heads”。这里“接近恒等”很关键：如果一开始就做强混合，训练可能不稳定，也容易破坏原有注意力结构；近恒等初始化更像是在 GQA-2 的基础上逐步学出组内头部专门化。作者从训练后矩阵的直接可视化里观察到，Premix 学到的是 group-conditioned query specialization，也就是同组内不同虚拟头会形成有结构的差异，而不是无意义的线性扰动。

第二部分是 Linear Postmix。仅靠组内 Premix 还不够，因为 KV heads 只有 2，跨组的信息通道仍然受限。Postmix 在 attention 输出后施加一个低秩 identity-residual 变换 I + AB^T，其中秩 r 取 Hq'/2，例如 1.7B 模型里 r=4。这个设计的意图是用很小的额外参数和计算，把不同头、不同组之间的特征再融合一次。作者把它解释为 structured low-rank cross-head communication。与 MFA 通过增大 head dimension 来补容量不同，VHA 不去扩大每个头的宽度，而是在头之间做便宜的线性耦合，因此训练和 prefill FLOPs 不会上升，反而因为物理 query heads 减半而下降。

一个很漂亮的工程点是：Premix 和 Postmix 都是纯线性操作，没有非线性，也不依赖 token 位置或上下文状态，因此在推理时可以分别吸收到 WQ 和 WO 中。吸收后，线上模型就是一个标准 GQA-2 结构，完全复用现有 kernel 和 serving 优化，不引入额外 runtime overhead。这一点把它和很多“训练时好看、部署时麻烦”的注意力变体区分开了。

从对比关系看，VHA 与 GQA 的区别是：GQA 直接让更多 query heads 共享同一组 K/V，而 VHA 在共享前后都加了可学习线性补偿；与 MLA 的区别是：VHA 不做 latent KV 压缩，因此避免了 latent bottleneck 带来的质量损失；与 MFA 的区别是：VHA 不通过增大 head dim 来换质量，因此不会显著增加训练和 prefill 计算。40:T834,实验覆盖面比较完整。作者在四个基础规模上做了 4K context、50B token 预训练：0.6B、1.7B、4B dense，以及 8B-A1B MoE。结果是 VHA 在所有规模上都超过标准 GQA baseline，提升范围约为 +0.05% 到 +0.81%。这里绝对数值看起来不大，但要注意比较对象已经是很强的 GQA，而且 VHA 同时把 KV cache 压下去了。

以 1.7B 为例，GQA-8 的 KV cache 是每层每 token 4KB（BF16），直接降到 GQA-2 后变成 1KB，但会带来约 1.00% 的质量下降。MLA 的 cache 约 1.12KB，质量在多个尺度上最低。MFA 也能做到 1KB cache，质量接近 GQA-8，但在 1.7B、序列长度 4096 时训练和 prefill FLOPs 增加 49.8%。VHA 则在保持 1KB 级别 cache 的同时，相比 GQA-8 还把训练和 prefill FLOPs 降低了 7.9%，并且质量超过标准 GQA baseline。这正是论文所谓同时改进三角形三个顶点的证据。

更重要的是工业级验证。作者在 30B-A3B MoE、500B token、8K context 的设置下，VHA 在 12 个 base-model benchmark 上比 MLA 高 0.70%，比 GQA-4 高 2.60%。这说明方法在更大模型和更长训练下仍然成立，而不是小模型偶然收益。另一个 matched 10B-A1B MoE 对比把结论延伸到 128K context，在更激进的 KV 压缩下，VHA 仍保持优势。

论文还做了组件消融。结论是 Premix 和 Postmix 缺一不可：只做其中一个，无法补齐双重压缩带来的表达损失。作者还直接检查训练后的 Premix/Postmix 矩阵结构，发现前者呈现组条件化的头专门化，后者呈现低秩但有结构的跨头通信，这让方法不只是经验上有效，也有一定可解释性。

如果从预训练角度看，最值得注意的数字不是单个 benchmark 分，而是：在 50B 到 500B token 的训练规模上，VHA 没有表现出随着规模增大而收益消失；同时它把线上 cache 压到 GQA-2 级别，却没有像纯 GQA-2 或 MLA 那样明显掉质量。这说明它抓住的不是小模型欠拟合补丁，而是 attention 参数化里一个更稳定的自由度。41:T8b7,Virtual Head Attention starts from an aggressive compression setting: only 2 KV heads, and only half as many physical query heads as the baseline. This immediately reduces both KV cache and attention compute, but it also removes a large amount of head diversity. VHA restores that diversity through two lightweight linear modules.

The first is Q Premix. Within each KV group, Premix applies a near-identity linear transformation to the reduced set of physical query heads, effectively expanding them into a richer set of virtual query heads. The near-identity design is important. It keeps the model close to a stable GQA-2 parameterization early in training, while allowing the network to gradually learn structured specialization among heads that share the same KV pair. The authors’ matrix inspection suggests that this is exactly what happens: Premix learns group-conditioned query specialization rather than arbitrary mixing.

The second is Linear Postmix. Even with better within-group query diversity, using only 2 KV heads still limits cross-group interaction. Postmix therefore applies a low-rank identity-residual transformation, I + AB^T, to the attention output. The rank is small, for example r = Hq'/2 and r = 4 at the 1.7B scale. This gives the model a cheap way to fuse information across heads and groups after attention, without increasing head dimension or introducing nonlinear runtime structure. The paper interprets this as structured low-rank cross-head communication.

A major engineering advantage is that both modules are purely linear. Premix can be folded into the query projection matrix WQ, and Postmix into the output projection WO at inference time. After folding, the deployed model is just a standard GQA-2 model. This means VHA inherits existing inference kernels and serving optimizations from frameworks such as vLLM and SGLang with zero additional runtime overhead.

Relative to prior methods, the distinctions are clean. Compared with standard GQA, VHA adds learnable compensation before and after shared-KV attention. Compared with MLA, it avoids a latent KV bottleneck. Compared with MFA, it does not increase head dimension and therefore avoids the large training/prefill FLOP increase.42:T705,The paper reports matched pretraining experiments at four scales under 4K context and 50B tokens: 0.6B, 1.7B, 4B dense, and 8B-A1B MoE. VHA consistently outperforms the standard GQA baseline at every scale, with gains ranging from about +0.05% to +0.81%. The absolute gains are modest, but the comparison is against already strong baselines while simultaneously reducing cache and compute.

The 1.7B case is especially informative. GQA-8 uses 4 KB of KV cache per layer per token in BF16. GQA-2 reduces that to 1 KB, but causes roughly a 1.00% quality drop. MLA reaches about 1.12 KB cache but gives the weakest quality among the compared methods. MFA also reaches 1 KB cache and gets close to GQA-8 quality, but increases training and prefill FLOPs by 49.8% at sequence length 4096. VHA keeps the cache at the compressed level, lowers training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9% relative to GQA-8, and still beats the standard GQA baseline in quality.

The industrial-scale result is even more important. On a 30B-A3B MoE model trained on 500B tokens with 8K context, VHA outperforms MLA by 0.70% and GQA-4 by 2.60% on a 12-benchmark base-model suite. A separate matched 10B-A1B MoE comparison extends the advantage to 128K context under more aggressive KV compression. This suggests the method scales in both model size and context length.

The component ablations show that neither Premix nor Postmix alone is sufficient. The matrix analyses are also useful: Premix learns structured specialization within KV groups, while Postmix learns low-rank but nontrivial cross-head communication. From a pretraining perspective, the key takeaway is that the gains do not disappear as training scale increases from 50B to 500B tokens, which makes the method more credible than a small-scale optimization artifact.43:T690,Read the paper in four passes. First, study the introduction carefully. The quantitative framing of the “impossible triangle” is essential: GQA-8 has strong quality but large cache, GQA-2 is cheap but weak, MLA compresses but loses quality, and MFA recovers quality at a large compute cost. Without that baseline map, the value of VHA is easy to underestimate.

Second, read the method section closely. Focus on how Q Premix is parameterized, why it is near-identity, and how it reconstructs virtual head diversity from fewer physical query heads. Then examine Linear Postmix and its low-rank identity-residual form. The important design question is not just what these modules do, but why they are placed before attention on queries and after attention on outputs, and why they are kept strictly linear. The answer is deployment: only this design can be folded into standard GQA weights with no inference overhead.

Third, inspect the main result tables, especially the 1.7B and 30B-A3B comparisons. The 1.7B setup makes the cache/FLOP/quality trade-off concrete. The 30B-A3B result tells you whether the method survives industrial-scale training. Also check the 128K long-context evaluation to verify that the advantage is not limited to short context.

Finally, read the ablations and matrix visualizations. These sections explain what Premix and Postmix are each compensating for, and whether the learned transformations have stable structure rather than acting as arbitrary extra parameters. If you are considering implementation or adaptation, pay attention to the appendix details on FLOP accounting, head configurations at different scales, and the exact MoE settings.44:T537,The method compresses generation in fixed 512-token blocks. After a block is completed, learned pause tokens attend to that block and store a summary in their own KV entries. These pause tokens do not emit output tokens. Once their KV entries are written, the original block cache is freed, and later tokens attend to the pause-token code rows instead. The training objective remains next-token prediction, so future prediction loss teaches the code rows what information to preserve. Three design choices are central. First, the code rows are assigned positions inside the block they replace, rather than being appended after it; this keeps the positional geometry closer to the original history under positional embeddings. Second, cache budget is allocated across layers according to measured value, instead of using a uniform per-layer budget. Third, compression is performed over relatively large blocks, reducing repeated lossy compression and overhead. Compared with LightThinker or Breadcrumbs-style memory-token compression, the contribution is not just adding learned memory tokens, but making them work in long competition-math generations through position, layer-budget, and block-size design. Compared with text-summary methods such as MEMENTO, it avoids an external annotation pipeline for writing and refining summaries.45:T419,The experiments cover Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 14B, with detailed results on Qwen3-8B-Base and post-trained Qwen3-8B. On Qwen3-8B-Base, RoleQ-T reaches 1.59 bpw with WikiText2 perplexity 11.33, seven-task zero-shot average 60.3, and five-shot MMLU 47.6, using only a few GPU-hours for conversion. With Fisher-selected secondary planes, 2.16 bpw improves to perplexity 9.30, zero-shot 65.9, and MMLU 62.8. On the post-trained Qwen3-8B, 1.99 bpw surpasses CAT-Q on all three reported measures while using 0.28 more bpw.
