Fisher selection for the second plane beats random by 6.2 MMLU points and Hessian × weight by 9.0 points on the post-trained 8B setting.46:T4ab,The key idea is to rewrite attention statistics so they can be accumulated or recovered within FlashAttention’s computation path.
- The paper distinguishes statistics (per-head quantities returned by kernels) from features (host-side aggregations used by a classifier).
- Using FlashAttention’s online softmax state (running max m, normalizer ℓ, accumulated output O) and the stored LSE, it classifies statistics into four exact computation tiers:
  (1) accumulate inside the tiled pass with bounded state (near-free),
  (2) a fixed number of post-pass sparse lookups by re-evaluating a few scores and recovering weights via LSE,
  (3) a second tiled pass over scores (still avoiding dense materialization),
  (4) statistics that truly require dense materialization.
- Implementation: Triton kernels extending FlashAttention-2 forward to emit the statistics needed by five published detectors (Lookback Lens, LLM-Check, RAUQ, INTRYGUE, SinkProbe), packaged as an attention backend for integration.
The design trade-off is explicit: keep statistics exact, prioritize tier (1)/(2) for common detectors, and offer tier (3) as a controlled extra pass rather than falling back to O(L^2) memory.47:T7e1,方法从注意力输出扰动的精确表达式出发。对给定 query q，完整 cache 下的注意力输出是 a=Σ_i p_i v_i。若删去索引集合 J，对应输出变成 a_-J，扰动是 Δ(J)=a_-J-a。作者先写出这个扰动与被删 token 的总注意力质量 P_J 以及 value residual 的关系。单 token 情况下有一个很直观的式子：Δ({j}) = p_j/(1-p_j) · (a - v_j)。这说明删一个 token 的影响不只取决于它的 attention weight p_j，也取决于它的 value 向量和当前输出 a 的偏差。如果 v_j 很接近 a，即便 attention 不低，删掉它也未必伤害大；反过来，一个 attention 中等但方向独特的 value 可能更关键。

难点在于多 token 联合删除时，最优集合选择是组合问题。DropKV 的核心是 decoupling：把联合扰动最小化近似成独立的 per-token 评分，再按分数保留或删除。论文里称之为 Decoupled Residual-Output Perturbation。直观上，它用单 token 扰动代理多 token 选择，把原本互相耦合的决策拆开，从而把复杂度降到线性级别。作者进一步给出 near-optimality 保证：在 cone condition 下，这个 decoupled proxy 与原 NP-hard 最优解只差一个常数因子。这里的 cone condition 可以理解为被选 value residual 在几何上不会严重相互抵消，方向大致处于同一锥体内。这个条件不是纯理论摆设，作者在 Llama-3.1-8B、Mistral-7B-512K、Qwen2.5-7B-1M 上做了经验验证。

工程实现上，DropKV 的另一个重点是 kernelization。很多 query-aware 或 output-aware 方法理论上合理，但需要显式构造大 attention matrix，prefill 阶段内存开销很大。作者用 fused Triton kernels 在线计算 eviction scores，避免 materialize attention matrix，把 128K 长度下 scoring kernel 的 scratch memory 从约 9GB 压到约 17MB。这个量级差异很关键，因为它决定方法能否在真实长上下文服务里启用，而不是只在离线实验里成立。48:T87b,The method starts from the exact perturbation of the attention output. For a query q, the full-cache attention output is a = Σ_i p_i v_i. If a set J of tokens is evicted, the new output is a_-J and the shift is Δ(J) = a_-J - a. The paper derives how this perturbation depends on the total removed attention mass P_J and on value residuals relative to the original output. The single-token case is especially revealing: Δ({j}) = p_j / (1 - p_j) · (a - v_j). This immediately shows why attention-only scoring is incomplete. A token can have nontrivial attention but still be safe to remove if its value is close to the current output; conversely, a token with moderate attention can be important if its value points in a distinctive direction.

The hard part is multi-token selection, which is combinatorial. DropKV’s main idea is decoupling: replace the joint optimization over eviction sets with independent per-token perturbation scores. The paper calls this Decoupled Residual-Output Perturbation. Intuitively, it uses single-token perturbation as a proxy for the multi-token objective, breaking the coupling between decisions and reducing the complexity to linear time. The authors then prove a near-optimality result: under a cone condition, the decoupled proxy matches the NP-hard optimum up to a constant multiplicative factor. The cone condition roughly says that the relevant residual vectors do not cancel each other arbitrarily and lie within a bounded geometric cone. Importantly, the paper does not leave this as a purely formal assumption; it empirically checks the condition on Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-512K, and Qwen2.5-7B-1M.

The implementation side is equally important. Many query-aware or output-aware methods require materializing large attention matrices, which makes prefill expensive. DropKV uses fused Triton kernels to compute eviction scores on the fly, avoiding attention-matrix materialization. At sequence length 128K, this reduces scoring-kernel scratch memory from about 9 GB to about 17 MB. That difference is large enough to determine whether a method is usable in real long-context serving rather than only in offline experiments.49:T53c,The experiments cover three long-context models: Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-512K, and Qwen2.5-7B-1M. The main benchmarks are RULER and LongBench, with cache budgets of 5% and 10%, which are fairly aggressive compression settings. The headline result is that DropKV achieves the best accuracy among both query-aware and output-aware eviction baselines while also delivering the lowest latency. More notably, in matched-batch prefill it is reported to be faster than the dynamic-cache baseline, which suggests the method is not merely trading quality for speed; the kernel design is removing a real prefill bottleneck.

The most striking engineering number is the memory reduction: at n = 128K, scratch memory for score computation drops from roughly 9 GB to roughly 17 MB. The paper also empirically validates the cone condition to support the relevance of its approximation guarantee on real models.

When reading the experiments closely, three comparisons matter most. First, compare against attention-only methods to see where value-aware scoring helps most. Second, compare against more complex output-perturbation baselines to separate gains from the proxy itself versus gains from better implementation. Third, inspect the degradation curves across cache budgets to judge whether the method remains stable under very low retention rates.4a:T46c,A good way to read this paper is formula first, approximation second, implementation third. Start with the perturbation derivation in the method section, especially the single-token formula; that is the key intuition for the whole paper. Then read the decoupling argument and the approximation guarantee to understand what is being approximated, what interactions are discarded, and why the resulting score is tractable. Even if you are not theory-focused, read the explanation and empirical validation of the cone condition; otherwise it is hard to judge where the guarantee applies. Finally, read the Triton-kernel section and the latency/memory tables, because much of the paper’s practical value comes from implementation.

If you only have 20 minutes, read the introduction, the derivation around the main theorem, the main benchmark table, and the scratch-memory comparison. For a deeper pass, two questions are worth probing: whether per-token decoupling introduces systematic bias across heads, layers, or query distributions, and how easily the method composes with quantization, paged KV caches, or speculative decoding.4b:T72b,RoLaQ combines rotation learning and range calibration. The starting point is an error analysis: if the dequantized latent differs from the original by e, then the induced key and value projection errors are governed by quadratic forms involving W_K and W_V. The authors trace-normalize the two projection energies and sum them into a joint matrix H, which measures how sensitive each latent direction is to shared K/V distortion. Empirically, the leading half of H's eigenvectors captures 62% to 75% of the projection energy across models and layers, so RoLaQ restricts rotation learning to a compact subspace defined by this joint geometry rather than searching over the full latent space.

The second ingredient is coupled threshold-gain learning. RoLaQ does not keep the quantizer range fixed while only optimizing the rotation. Instead, it jointly learns a per-layer threshold whose value also determines the reconstruction gain. This matters because at 2 bits, the rotation changes the latent distribution seen by the quantizer, while the quantization boundaries and dequantization scale jointly determine the effective reconstruction response. Optimizing only one side leaves a mismatch between assignment and readout behavior.

Training uses frozen model weights. Supervision comes from two sources: a prediction-level KL to a BF16 teacher over next-token distributions, and an attention-output reconstruction loss that directly constrains layerwise attention outputs. The latter is important because final-logit supervision alone can hide harmful intermediate distortions. On the systems side, the serving implementation packs the latent cache into INT2, fuses cache writes, optimizes the attention path, and absorbs the read-side rotation into MLA projections so that inference does not pay an extra standalone rotation cost.4c:T618,The evaluation covers three MLA models: DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Moonlight-16B-A3B, and MiniCPM3-4B, across six benchmarks. The main result is that RoLaQ achieves the best average accuracy among compared 2-bit methods both with and without token protection. Without token protection, it improves over the strongest baseline by 1.1 to 3.8 points on average, which is a meaningful gain at this compression level.

The long-context result is also important. On RULER retrieval at 8K and 16K, the gains persist beyond the 4K calibration context, suggesting that the method is not merely overfitting a short calibration window but is improving the underlying quantization geometry.

The serving numbers are strong for the target setting. On DeepSeek-V2-Lite with a 256K input on a single A100 80GB, the packed 2-bit cache reaches 3.96x the BF16 cache capacity at the same memory budget and 2.51x decode throughput, while also reducing first-token tail latency. Calibration itself takes about 30 minutes on one A100, so the offline cost is modest.

The ablations are the most informative part. Rotation-only and range-only variants both underperform joint optimization, supporting the claim that error direction and reconstruction scale must be calibrated together. The K/V-guided subspace outperforms less structured rotation search, which validates the MLA-specific geometry argument. Adding attention-output supervision improves stability and quality over using prediction KL alone, especially in the 2-bit regime where intermediate-layer distortions accumulate quickly.4d:T485,The main setup uses a frozen Qwen2.5-1.5B receiver with 28 layers and grouped-query attention with group size 6. The probe is split-context factual recall derived from SQuAD. The sender reads a passage containing the answer; the receiver sees the same passage with the answer masked plus the question; the system is scored by whether greedy decoding over eight tokens contains the answer. The reported run uses n=200 items. Two anchors define the scale: the masked native cache gives 0.180 accuracy, and the receiver’s own unmasked native cache gives 0.665. When the receiver’s cache is perturbed, accuracy is already at the floor at cosine 0.9999, drops to 0.120 at cosine 0.999, and falls to 0.005 at cosine 0.995. In contrast, a genuine cache produced by the same model on the unmasked passage has achieved cosine 0.9949 yet transfers at 0.445. This reversal is the central empirical point: a geometrically closer cache can be unusable, while a more distant on-forward-pass cache can work. Sender-side substitution remains near the floor in the tested regime, while augmentation avoids the same constraint and can approach the native-cache reference.4e:T664,The technical contribution has three parts. First, the paper introduces a simple cost model for remote KV hits. It uses per-token KV size s and GPU prefill rate R to define a break-even bandwidth B*=sR, plus a fixed per-hit overhead T0. The interpretation is straightforward: if the effective remote-tier bandwidth and fixed latency do not clear that threshold, a cache hit is not worth taking. Second, the authors redesign KV storage for PCP with MLA. In the original LMCache setup, only worker 0 stores and loads MLA KV because tensor-parallel ranks hold the same latent KV. Under PCP, however, all ranks advance in lockstep, so concentrating remote I/O on one rank creates a bottleneck. The paper replaces this with a sharded MLA KV store, where chunk storage, lookup, and loading are statically partitioned by rank. Rank r of every engine talks to its own server instance, which avoids extra cluster protocols and client-side hashing while preserving cross-engine reuse. The paper also proves that the scheduler’s existing minimum-over-ranks lookup still returns the longest cached prefix. Third, the execution path is repaired. Synchronous loading is replaced with asynchronous loading so that hit processing no longer blocks the engine step. The authors also fix three client bugs, including a lost-completion race and a missing-key read that could stall indefinitely, and add regression tests. The key idea is not an API trick but moving remote-hit handling off the blocking critical path while keeping the load protocol compatible with collectives: every rank issues the same collectives, avoiding deadlocks and inconsistency.4f:T4de,The experiments are the strongest part of the paper because they are driven by production trace replay rather than only synthetic microbenchmarks. In the original deployment, enabling remote L2 increased p99 TTFT for 16k prompts from 3.96s to 17.3s, and for 32k prompts from 6.06s to 25.0s, while median latency stayed roughly unchanged. Isolated replay shows why: a 16k prompt takes 0.31s to recompute but 0.88s to load from L2. On the same B300 node, GPU prefill runs at about 52.2k tokens/s, so the remote path is simply too slow. The queueing effect is even more important. Under a hit-heavy synchronous workload, once arrival rate times per-hit service time exceeds one, the engine becomes unstable: median latency grows from 3.52s to 52.30s within six minutes while GPU utilization is only 7%, showing that the bottleneck is entirely outside compute. After the fixes, p99 on a hit-heavy production trace drops from 83.32s to 0.67s, a 124x reduction, with 98.5% of prompt tokens served from L2. The sharded store improves prefill throughput by 14% to 34%, and a five-node disaggregated deployment meets the workload SLA. The cost model is also validated on configurations not used for fitting, which makes it more than a one-off explanation.50:T442,RoPERelay takes a selector-produced sparse KV cache and the source positions of the retained states. It sorts retained states by their original chronological order and assigns compact, order-preserving RoPE coordinates, removing the gaps created by evicted tokens. Since cached keys already include RoPE phase at the original positions, the method applies an inverse rotation to remove the old phase and then re-rotates each key at its new compact coordinate. This directly edits the selected cache keys and avoids rerunning the historical context. For layers and physical KV heads with different retained lengths, RoPERelay aligns their endpoints using the maximum retained length M, so the current question and subsequent generation start from a shared positional boundary. This is better than starting every head at zero, which would create inconsistent distances from different heads to the current query. The method also separates membership from organization: selector scores decide which states to keep, while source order decides the positional order in which those states are read.51:T75f,The main contribution is not a new model but a unified benchmark and protocol. System1-Arena represents each static example or environment step as a decision request r=(s,Q). The state s is a small set of named text fields, such as a message, a code diff, or a rendered webpage. Q is a set of typed questions over the same state. Questions are boolean, choice, or score. Each question includes instructions, and each option includes a description, so models do not rely on dataset-specific prompting. The output is a probability distribution over options for each question, not free-form text.

Several design choices matter. First, the interface is shared across model families. Dedicated System-1 models, autoregressive LLMs, and even diffusion LMs are all mapped into the same probability-based API. For open autoregressive and diffusion models, the authors provide a method to derive decision probabilities from answer tokens, which is important because it makes otherwise incompatible model families comparable. Second, the benchmark evaluates not only accuracy but also Brier score, since calibrated probabilities are central for thresholding, escalation, and risk-sensitive deployment. Third, it includes closed-loop environments and a real-time protocol in which the environment continues to evolve during inference according to each model’s measured latency. That turns latency from a side metric into part of the task definition.

The benchmark is broad: 92,125 typed questions across 105 tasks from 268 public sources in 16 domains, plus 138 closed-loop environments from 18 families, including web shopping, SWE-style coding control, robotics, games, and driving. This is not just a bundle of existing classification datasets. The benchmark standardizes instructions, option semantics, label sources, and environment feedback into a common probabilistic decision framework.52:T7e5,The evaluation covers 30 models: 7 closed LLMs, 13 open LLMs, and 10 System-1 models. On non-agentic tasks, Jev and Decision-2.0-Vega-27B reach 72.6% and 73.0% accuracy, slightly above GPT-6 Luna at 71.2%. They also provide better-calibrated probabilities and lower latency. The paper reports Jev at roughly $0.05 per 1,000 requests, which highlights the practical advantage of specialized decision models for high-throughput workloads.

The gains are task-dependent. The gap between strong System-1 models and the best LLMs is smallest on filtering, grouping, ranking, retrieval, and dialogue tasks. System-1 models remain weaker on knowledge and forecasting tasks. That pattern suggests that single-pass decision models are well suited to local discrimination and structured selection, but less suited to tasks that require broader knowledge integration or implicit multi-step reasoning.

Reasoning models still set the upper bound. Claude Opus 5.5 reaches 81.1% on non-agentic tasks, but at about 70 times the cost of a fast LLM. Among open models, Qwen3.8-27B reaches 75.6% when given a few hundred reasoning tokens per question, surpassing Jev in accuracy but producing less calibrated probabilities. This is an important result: explicit reasoning can improve top-1 accuracy without necessarily improving probability quality.

On agentic tasks, the paper separates single-step decision accuracy from long-horizon success. For single-step tasks, Decision-2.0-Vega-27B, Jev, and Qwen3.5-9B all reach 67.8% accuracy, showing that local action selection can be competitive across model types. On long-horizon tasks, Gemma-4-31B achieves the highest success rate at 32.9%, while the four small System-1 models reach at most 3.1%. This indicates a major weakness in long-range planning and recovery. The OpenAI Decisions API is faster and better calibrated than GPT-6 Luna, but achieves lower long-horizon success, reinforcing that calibrated local decisions and successful sequential control are not the same capability.53:T5ab,This one is worth a close read. 数据设计上，FEB-30 包含 30 条 fact-evolution trajectories，覆盖 6 个诊断类别和 3 个难度等级。6 个类别分别对应外在 QA 评测看不清的不同失败模式：
1. C1 LLM Compensation：memory 状态错了，但模型仍可能答对。
2. C2 Retrieval Bottleneck：memory 对了，但 retrieval 因词汇不匹配或抽象层级差异而失败。
3. C3 Classification Accuracy：系统是否正确判断新观察是 create、update、reinforce 还是 conflict。
4. C4 Synthesis Quality：多来源观察是否被正确合并成事实，哪些该合并，哪些应分开。
5. C5 Temporal Correctness：事实随时间演化、撤回、漂移时，memory state 是否保持正确时序。
6. C6 Multi-Author Attribution：不同作者来源对 corroboration、冲突处理、置信度整合的影响是否被正确建模。

难度上，L1 接近表面匹配，目标 claim 几乎原文出现；L2 把 claim 埋进更真实的文档上下文；L3 则要求从多句组合中推断，并加入较多干扰内容。

这篇工作的关键创新不是类别枚举，而是数据生成范式。作者采用 paradigm inversion：不是先收集文档再人工标注事实，而是先定义每条 trajectory 在每个 state 应该有哪些 atomic claims、如何演化，再据此生成文档。这样 ground truth 从一开始就是确定的。文中还提到 multi-model rotation 和 3-judge verification，用来控制生成文档质量与事实一致性，减少单模型模板化偏差。

评测上，作者把 intrinsic 和 extrinsic 两套指标并列。intrinsic evaluation 直接比较 memory store 内容与该阶段真值，指标包括 claim coverage、update detection、false update rate 等；extrinsic evaluation 则仍保留 QA accuracy。这样可以把“存错了”“没取到”“答错了”拆开看。论文的立场不是用 intrinsic 替代 extrinsic，而是把它作为 memory 组件的单元测试，与端到端 QA 形成互补。57:T8ac,The paper introduces FEB-30, a benchmark for fact evolution in agent memory, together with an intrinsic scoring framework.

FEB-30 contains 30 fact-evolution trajectories spanning 6 diagnostic categories and 3 difficulty levels. The categories are designed to isolate failure modes that extrinsic QA-based evaluation cannot disentangle:
1. C1, LLM Compensation: the memory state is wrong, but the model may still answer correctly.
2. C2, Retrieval Bottleneck: the memory state is correct, but retrieval fails because of lexical mismatch or abstraction mismatch.
3. C3, Classification Accuracy: whether the system correctly classifies observations as create, update, reinforce, or conflict.
4. C4, Synthesis Quality: whether evidence from multiple artifacts is merged into the right fact structure.
5. C5, Temporal Correctness: whether the memory state tracks temporal evolution, retraction, and drift correctly.
6. C6, Multi-Author Attribution: whether source identity is handled correctly in corroboration, conflict handling, and confidence updates.

Difficulty is controlled in a structured way. L1 is close to surface matching, with target claims appearing almost verbatim. L2 embeds claims in more realistic document context. L3 requires inference from multiple statements and includes substantial distractor content.

The most important design choice is what the authors call paradigm inversion. Instead of starting from documents and then annotating facts, they first define the exact atomic claims that should hold at each state of a trajectory, then generate documents from those trajectories. This makes the ground truth deterministic from the start. The pipeline also uses multi-model rotation and three-judge verification to reduce generator-specific artifacts and improve factual consistency.

Evaluation is split into intrinsic and extrinsic metrics. Intrinsic evaluation directly compares the memory store against the state-specific ground truth, using metrics such as claim coverage, update detection, and false update rate. Extrinsic evaluation keeps the usual QA accuracy. The point is not to replace end-to-end evaluation, but to complement it with a unit-test-like view of the memory component itself.58:T5bf,The central empirical result is straightforward: intrinsic and extrinsic evaluations diverge substantially. The paper reports an average gap of 16 percentage points, and 44% of trajectories show what the authors consider a meaningful divergence. This is the main evidence that QA accuracy alone is not a reliable measure of memory quality.

By construction, C1 and C2 are the clearest demonstrations of the problem. C1 produces cases where systems answer correctly despite broken memory. C2 produces cases where memory is correct but the final answer is wrong because retrieval fails. Categories C3 through C6 are more diagnostic of internal memory-pipeline behavior, including update classification, synthesis, temporal consistency, and source attribution. Two systems with similar QA scores can therefore have very different internal memory quality.

The provided material does not include the full system comparison tables, per-category scores, or judge agreement details. But the experimental goal is clear: not to rank systems by one aggregate score, but to show that intrinsic and extrinsic evaluation measure different things. A careful reader should verify three aspects in the full paper: the protocol for aligning memory-store contents with claim-level ground truth, the robustness of the document-generation and verification pipeline, and whether the category-specific error patterns are genuinely diagnostic rather than just reflecting overall model strength.59:T623,The contribution is a benchmark design, not a new model. The provided excerpt does not include the full leaderboard or all breakdowns, but it is already clear that current models remain weak at long-horizon scientific judgment.5f:T8c4,The core system is a multi-agent synthesis engine called Data World. A world is formalized as a four-tuple: dependency skeleton G, canonical state X, observed environment E, and recomputable phenomena I. G is a DAG whose nodes are variable clusters and whose edges encode generative relations such as monotonic, threshold, saturation, lagged, or interaction effects. This is not just a graph template; the edge annotations define how the world is generated. X is the latent canonical state, the objective world state that actually governs the phenomena of interest. E is produced by an observation map O that projects X into analyst-visible artifacts such as CSVs, spreadsheets, and logs, with imperfect observability, aggregation, missingness, and noise. I contains target phenomena that can be recomputed and checked from the generated world and, crucially, are intended to remain recoverable from E.

A key design choice is the staged multi-agent pipeline. Separate agent sessions handle world specification, state generation, file projection, task and rubric synthesis, and auditing, while exchanging read-only artifacts. This is meant to preserve consistency without letting later stages directly exploit hidden latent variables. The auditor is central: it verifies both that the intended relationships were instantiated and that the target phenomena remain recoverable from imperfect observations. That addresses two common failure modes in synthetic environments: latent mechanisms that disappear after projection, and tasks that become trivial because the signal is too directly exposed.

Task generation is paired with fine-grained rubrics rather than single gold answers. The rubrics distinguish correct computation from correct analytical insight and evidence use. This gives structured rewards for evaluation and RL. The training setup is world-disjoint, so train and test tasks come from disjoint worlds rather than different prompts over the same latent template. The paper then uses these rubric rewards for RL-zero training, without distilling trajectories from stronger teacher models, to produce DataWorld-35B-A3B. That makes the work especially relevant to current interest in verifier- or environment-based training signals.60:T647,The engine produces two main assets. DataWorld-Bench contains 100 tasks from 50 held-out worlds across 16 domains, with human-preference-based curation for question realism. The RL training set contains 2,135 tasks from 1,037 worlds that are disjoint from the benchmark worlds. The scale is moderate, but the emphasis is on world-level diversity and split hygiene rather than raw task count.

On evaluation, the authors test 10 frontier models and consistently observe a computation-versus-insight gap. Models can often perform local calculations, filtering, and aggregation, yet struggle more on identifying the underlying drivers, explaining why an outcome changed, or tracing downstream implications. This is an informative result because it shows that the bottleneck in data agents is not only tool use or table manipulation, but mechanism recovery under partial observation.

Stage I collects bug-fix commits and converts each (buggy → fixed) transformation into a reversed pair (fixed/golden code → buggy code), preserving repository context and test infrastructure so the injected bug is observable via failing tests. Stage II trains a bug-inducing model on these reversed transformations to generate bug-introducing patches in new code contexts, producing new repo-level task instances.

Two variants are proposed:
- SWE-at-Scale: directly generates bug-inducing patches from correct code.
- SWE-at-Scale+: additionally learns explicit natural-language bug patterns describing how to modify code to induce a bug, then realizes the patch from the pattern—aiming for more explicit, controllable bug logic at the cost of a harder generation problem.

Compared to SWE-smith/SWE-Synth/BugPilot, the key shift is from prompt-elicited priors to a trained distribution grounded in real fix transformations, designed to remain diverse under repeated sampling.63:T4b8,Methodologically, this is an evaluation argument backed by a controlled case study. The paper defines an access path as any transformation or recovery mechanism that changes how the same targeted information is queried or extracted while keeping the underlying information approximately fixed. Cross-lingual querying is chosen because it is a clean instance of this idea: semantics are largely preserved while surface form changes substantially.

The experiments use cTOFU, a multilingual extension of TOFU, with parallel synthetic factual associations in English, Chinese, Hindi, Italian, and Spanish, plus romanized Hindi and Chinese. The original forget/retain partitions are preserved. The study focuses on one-to-one unlearning: unlearn in one language, evaluate in another. The contribution is therefore not a new training recipe but a reframing of what unlearning evaluation should claim. Standard metrics such as Truth Ratio, KS-test-based forget quality, and utility preservation can show distribution-specific behavioral change, but they do not by themselves support a privacy claim. The paper argues that privacy-oriented evaluation should ask whether forgetting survives alternative access paths.64:T41c,From the provided full text, the empirical study uses the 10% forget split in cTOFU and evaluates with TOFU-style forget-quality and normalized model-utility metrics. The main result is qualitative but important: conclusions about unlearning success change when the same information is queried through different languages or scripts. A model family may look successfully unlearned under one language-specific evaluation and still reveal the same information under another language or romanized script. That means monolingual evaluation can materially overestimate forgetting strength.

The paper also makes three broader empirical points. First, this is observed across multiple multilingual model families rather than a single isolated model. Second, the gap appears not only across languages but also across script variants, which is useful because it keeps semantics even more tightly controlled. Third, utility preservation is orthogonal to privacy: retaining general capability does not imply that the targeted information has become inaccessible.65:T433,ViSiP-Bench builds rare-but-real cases where visual evidence conflicts with likely language priors. It covers six categories: Physical Properties, Time & Space, Scientific & Mathematic, Customs & Culture, Psychology Cognition, and Function Cognition. The construction pipeline enumerates 200 priors per category with Claude Opus 4.7, yielding 1,200 priors, generates rare real-world counter-scenarios, collects web images, supplements missing cases with GPT-Image-2 and Nano Banana 2 in multiple visual styles, and applies human review to the multiple-choice questions. The evaluation protocol is model-aware: each model is first queried without an image to obtain its blank-condition answer; after adding the image, PAR measures how often the model adheres to that prior answer, while VIG measures the confidence shift induced by visual input. Items already answered correctly without the image are filtered. The mitigation method, MAPS, adds targeted factual exposure to rare-but-real scenarios, aiming to soften excessive prior reliance without suppressing priors broadly.66:T412,URW has an offline calibration stage and an online weighting stage.
- Offline: For each criterion judgment, URW queries the same verifier using a fixed pool of paraphrased judgment templates. Template-to-template variability provides a soft uncertainty proxy even under deterministic decoding. Using a small calibration set with gold labels, URW measures how this soft signal correlates with correctness.
- Online: For each new criterion, URW converts the soft signal into a split-conformal p-value, and uses that p-value directly as the aggregation weight for the criterion in a weighted-sum rubric score.
The key design choice is conformal calibration: it yields distribution-free coverage control, framed here as controlling the probability of assigning spuriously low weight to a correct judgment. Compared to prior work, URW is criterion-level (not only response-level), training-free (no uncertainty head/probe), and compatible with single-verifier, zero-temperature deployments (unlike sampling-based consistency or committee methods).67:T447,For pretraining research, this is a useful idea paper rather than a must-read. Its main contribution is a practical alternative to explicit paired cross-modal supervision: use text as an intermediate semantic space, rely on pretrained contrastive encoders for cross-modal priors, and learn bridge modules that map proxy descriptions into representations consumable by the language model. This matters because in many realistic settings, single-modality or modality-text data are abundant, while high-quality jointly sampled non-text data are the real bottleneck. The paper is also careful about its claim: MSP does not remove cross-modal priors altogether. It still depends on CLIP/CLAP-like encoders and modality-text supervision. So the reduction is in the need for real paired non-text supervision, not in the need for pretrained cross-modal structure. For native multimodal pretraining, the key takeaway is that text-mediated alignment may be sufficient for some forms of modality composition, though likely more at the semantic level than at fine-grained temporal or spatial correspondence.68:T646,The method has four components: frozen modality encoders, modality-specific projectors, text-to-modality bridges, and a language model. The encoders are pretrained contrastive models, such as CLIP-like vision encoders and CLAP-like audio encoders. Training proceeds in two stages. Stage one is per-modality projector training, where standard modality-text data are used to train projectors so that each modality can be mapped into a shared language embedding space. Stage two is self-play composition training, which is the core idea. Given one observed modality, say an image, the system generates proxy text for an unseen modality, for example a textual description of what the corresponding audio might contain. This proxy text is encoded by a pretrained text encoder and then passed through a bridge plus an MLP projector to produce a representation in the shared language space. During training, the model sees the real observed modality together with the proxy-derived representation of the missing modality, but never the true image-audio pair. The goal is not to reconstruct the unseen modality exactly. The goal is to provide a stable semantic anchor that lets the model learn how to combine modalities in the shared space. Compared with approaches based on shared encoders or modular concatenation, MSP explicitly uses text as the bridge and adds a learned calibration layer to correct the mismatch between proxy-text embeddings and real modality embeddings. That calibration is important because raw text-encoder outputs do not naturally follow the same distribution as actual modality features.69:T601,The main experimental setting is strong and clean: no real audio-vision pairs are used in training, only image-text and audio-text supervision, while evaluation requires joint multimodal reasoning. The paper reports competitive and in some cases leading results on standard multimodal benchmarks, supporting the claim that zero-shot modality composition can emerge. The most informative findings are in the ablations rather than in any single leaderboard number. First, removing the learned bridge weakens alignment between proxy-derived embeddings and real modality representations, and multimodal reasoning performance drops accordingly. Second, proxy quality matters: if the generated proxy text is vague or semantically unstable, the model tends to fall back to single-modality reasoning or language priors. Third, the method benefits heavily from the pretrained contrastive encoders, which means MSP is better understood as composition learning on top of existing cross-modal geometry rather than fully unsupervised multimodal grounding. Since the prompt does not include the full result tables, the most important things to verify in the paper are the training data scale, the exact encoders used, the language model size, the gap to paired-data baselines on each benchmark, and the size of the bridge/proxy ablation effects. If the gap to paired supervision is small, the method is more broadly interesting; if it is large, the approach is likely better suited to coarse semantic composition than tightly coupled perception tasks.6a:T4c9,The method casts three spatial output types as classification over candidate sets. Multiple-choice spatial relations are already finite. Numerical prediction is handled by discretizing a range into bins. Point prediction is handled by discretizing the image into regions. The model encodes the observation, question, and candidate descriptions, then uses the final attention layer’s pretrained query and key projections to score candidates, followed by a softmax. No extra prediction head or trainable readout parameters are added. To keep the candidate set manageable, scalar prediction uses up to two refinement stages, while single-point prediction uses three stages. For point prediction, the selected region is cropped and re-encoded in later stages to recover local visual detail. Multi-point prediction is handled by conditional tree expansion using the same trained point predictor. During training, the multi-stage supervision is packed into one teacher-forced causal forward pass, and stage losses are averaged per question so that multi-stage examples do not dominate the objective. The training system also uses global length grouping and cross-GPU load balancing to reduce padding waste and workload imbalance.6b:T610,FeaTok has two main components. First, it replaces pixel reconstruction as the training signal for the discrete representation with feature reconstruction. Instead of the conventional encoder-quantizer-pixel-decoder pipeline, the tokenizer is trained with an encoder, a quantizer, and a feature decoder that predicts patch-level features extracted from a frozen pretrained vision model. The paper studies several feature sources, including SigLIP, SigLIP2, DINOv2, and DINOv3. The important point is not that feature losses are added on top of pixel losses, but that feature-space supervision becomes the primary and exclusive signal for shaping the encoder and codebook. Second, image rendering is explicitly decoupled from representation learning. A separate image decoder is still trained to reconstruct pixels from the discrete tokens, but the tokens are detached before entering this renderer. Pixel losses therefore improve visual reconstruction without pulling the tokenizer back toward pixel-friendly but generator-unfriendly representations. The paper also introduces global-augmented generative modeling. A global image representation, such as a CLS token from the encoder, is discretized and generated before the patch tokens. This gives the autoregressive generator image-level context and improves spatial coherence and layout. Compared with earlier feature-target tokenizers, the distinctive move here is the full removal of pixel loss from the representation path, plus the detached renderer that preserves usability for image synthesis.6c:T619,The experimental story has three parts. First, tokenizer ablations show that feature-only training consistently produces better downstream generation than pixel-only or mixed pixel-plus-feature objectives across all four pretrained feature backbones tested: SigLIP, SigLIP2, DINOv2, and DINOv3. The paper also reports better spatial structure in the learned tokens, suggesting that the resulting discrete sequences are easier to model at object and layout level rather than only at local texture level. Second, on class-conditional ImageNet-1k generation, the paper evaluates with gFDr6 instead of a single Inception-space FID. gFDr6 averages Fréchet-distance ratios across six feature spaces, which makes the comparison less tied to one evaluator. At 256×256, FeaTok improves over the strongest discrete baselines by 29% without guidance and 25% with guidance. At 512×512, the gains become larger: relative to BAR, gFDr6 is reduced by 43% without guidance and 39% with guidance, compared with 32% and 25% at 256×256. The deepest idea in the paper is the operationalization of generative learnability as a tokenizer design target.6e:Ta01,方法从 KL-regularized policy optimization 的对偶结构出发。给定参考策略和温度参数，存在一个 Gibbs 形式的目标策略，使得“奖励减去相对参考策略的 KL 代价”在目标分布支持上呈常数。GGPO不去显式估计这个 Gibbs policy，也不做 importance weighting，而是利用同一 prompt 下 behavior policy 采到的一组响应，比较这些响应的 KL-adjusted reward 是否已经接近这种“常数化”条件。具体目标是最小化组内 KL-adjusted reward 的 log-mean-exp contrast。直观上，它不是像 AGRO 那样压缩 adjusted reward 的方差，也不是像 GRPO 那样直接做组内相对优势更新，而是在组内构造一个对高 adjusted-reward 响应更敏感、同时保持平滑性的对比目标。论文强调两个层面。
第一，on-policy 时，这个 population loss 恰好等于 KL-regularized optimality gap，也就是离正则化最优策略还有多远；这给了目标函数很干净的解释。第二，off-policy 时，不再追求无偏估计这个 population quantity，而是直接证明：在 coverage 条件下，有限组上的 raw loss 可以上界 learner 单次采样 reward 与 behavior best-of-K reward 之间的差距，外加若干显式项，包括正则项、reference-behavior mismatch、组大小和有限样本误差。这个思路和传统 off-policy 校正不同，它绕开了“先把 off-policy 目标估准，再优化”的路线，而是直接把训练时可观测的组损失和最终 reward benchmark 连起来。
论文还分析了 periodic reference refresh。固定 reference 时，Gibbs target 是固定的；如果周期性把 reference 刷新到当前 learner，目标会随轮次移动。作者证明：若每一轮都精确拟合对应的 Gibbs target，那么做 T 轮、每轮温度 β 的 refresh，等价于对初始 reference 做一次温度 β/T 的 Gibbs 更新。这个结果解释了为什么 refresh 能逐步把策略往更高 reward 区域推，而不是停留在单个固定 reference 定义的局部目标附近。对不精确更新，论文再给出有限数据下的 reward 保证，误差项由每轮 token 级 mismatch 和内层拟合误差累积控制。二值奖励和局部 reference 控制下，最终策略的单样本 reward 可以逼近初始策略的 best-of-K reward。和 AGRO 的关系也讲得比较清楚：两者共享同一个 regularized optimum，但 GGPO测的是组内 log-mean-exp contrast，AGRO测的是 adjusted reward variance，因此优化几何和有限组保证不同。6f:T9f9,The method is built from KL-regularized policy optimization and its Gibbs-form dual solution. Given a reference policy and temperature, there is a Gibbs target under which the KL-adjusted reward is constant on the support of the target distribution. GGPO does not estimate this target policy explicitly, and it does not apply learner-to-behavior importance weights. Instead, it uses groups of responses sampled from the behavior policy for the same prompt, and measures how far the within-group KL-adjusted rewards are from satisfying that constancy condition.
The resulting objective minimizes a log-mean-exp contrast of KL-adjusted rewards inside each response group. This is different from GRPO-style relative advantage updates, and also different from AGRO, which minimizes the variance of the same adjusted reward. The distinction matters: GGPO and AGRO share the same regularized optimum under common support, but they induce different optimization geometry and different finite-group guarantees.
The paper makes two theoretical moves. First, in the on-policy population setting, the GGPO objective is exactly the KL-regularized optimality gap. That gives the loss a clean interpretation: it is not merely a heuristic group contrast, but a direct measure of suboptimality under KL regularization. Second, in the off-policy setting, the analysis does not try to recover an unbiased estimate of that population quantity. Instead, it proves a direct reward comparison: under bounded coverage, the raw finite-group loss controls the gap between the learner’s expected reward from a single sample and the behavior policy’s best-of-K reward, up to explicit terms for regularization, reference-behavior mismatch, group size, and finite-sample error. This is the central conceptual shift of the paper.
A second major component is periodic reference refresh. With a fixed reference, GGPO optimizes toward a single Gibbs target. Refreshing the reference to the current learner changes the target across rounds. The paper shows that if each round exactly fits its Gibbs target, then T refresh rounds at temperature beta are equivalent to one Gibbs update at temperature beta/T. This explains why refresh can compound improvement rather than merely refine a fixed target. For imperfect updates, the paper derives finite-data guarantees in terms of aggregate tokenwise mismatch and inner optimization error. Under binary rewards and local reference control, the final policy’s single-sample reward can approach the best-of-K reward of the initial policy.70:T5ca,The empirical study is organized around three mismatch regimes: training-inference mismatch, controlled policy staleness, and offline training. Evaluation is on five mathematical reasoning benchmarks and two model sizes. The headline result stated in the paper is that GGPO outperforms both GRPO and AGRO under training-inference mismatch, and remains stable as synchronization delay increases from N=8 to N=128, whereas GRPO and AGRO degrade. At N=128, token-level TIS improves GRPO, but GGPO still performs better without relying on importance weighting.
The refresh ablation is especially important. The paper reports that periodic reference refresh substantially improves GGPO under the default training setup, which matches the theory: a fixed reference only defines one Gibbs target, while refresh allows successive rounds to build on previous progress. The experiments also appear designed to test the practical meaning of the theoretical terms, including mismatch severity, group-based supervision quality, and robustness under stale or offline data.

Expect roughly 1.5 to 2.5 hours for a careful read, with most of the time spent on the theory.72:T4cc,The system has three main components. First, Kaggle-MLE Factory converts historical Kaggle competitions into executable MLE tasks with task descriptions, public data, and metrics. The Interaction Harness preserves experimental state and candidate submissions while leaving action selection to the model, instead of forcing a fixed workflow. Second, hierarchical agentic SFT transfers tool use, coding, and MLE optimization skills through selected trajectories and segments. The selection is guided by execution outcomes, which is important because long trajectories are noisy: successful runs can contain unhelpful branches, and failed runs can still contain useful local behaviors. Third, Windowed Interaction Reinforcement Learning uses completed experiments as window boundaries. The decisions made since the previous experiment result form an execution window, and those decisions receive a shared outcome-based reward. This gives a denser and more causally aligned signal than final-task reward, while avoiding the overly local view of single-turn rewards. WIRL also uses local progress rewards, asynchronous rollout collection, and policy correction to handle expensive experiments and policy drift during online learning.73:T618,The authors do not propose a new detector. Instead, they reuse an existing three-tier candidate-generation pipeline and evaluate eight fully specified cleaning policies on top of it. Tier 1 performs exact and near-exact matching after normalization of whitespace, casing, and LaTeX macros. Tier 2 performs lexical matching using 13-gram and 8-gram coverage plus a 128-permutation MinHash/LSH Jaccard estimate. Tier 3 performs semantic retrieval with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and cosine similarity. A subset of lexical and semantic candidate pairs is then adjudicated by an existing LLM judge into same, subsumes, variant, or different. The eight policies differ in how much they trust exact matches, lexical heuristics, semantic thresholds, and LLM-judge outputs.

The strongest part of the paper is the evaluation design. The authors build a new independently and blindly dual-reviewed reference set of 594 training-benchmark pairs, split in advance into calibration and held-out partitions. The held-out split is disjoint not only in benchmark items but also in training-example clusters, so policy tuning is tested on genuinely unseen corpora and questions. They also sample 80 candidate-bearing training items and review every candidate edge attached to each item. That enables item-level false-removal measurement: a training item counts as wrongly removed only if none of its candidate edges is truly contaminating. This is more faithful than pair-level precision, which can overstate conservativeness when one item has both true and false candidate matches.74:T49f,The audit covers 16 open RLVR math corpora and 6 benchmarks: MATH-500, GSM8K test, AIME24, AIME25, AIME26, and AMC23. After normalization and corpus-specific deduplication, the study analyzes 1,673,514 corpus-specific training items corresponding to 1,197,691 unique underlying problem texts. Evaluation uses 594 manually reviewed pairs plus 80 fully resolved item-level samples.

The central empirical result is clear: the common heuristic “remove if semantic similarity exceeds a fixed threshold” becomes unreliable as the threshold is relaxed. Candidate-frame recall improves, but manual review shows that at permissive thresholds, most sampled removals are false removals. In other words, semantic retrieval is useful for candidate generation, but weak as a direct removal rule. The paper also reports the cost of each policy in retained corpus size and source-composition shift, showing that cleaning decisions affect not only how much data remains but also which sources remain. The abstract does not expose the full policy-by-policy table, but the paper’s contribution is less about naming a single best policy and more about making the trade-offs visible and auditable.75:T887,方法名叫 Mosaic，核心是两层优化信号。

第一层是 session-aware trajectory-level advantage estimation。普通 broadcasting 做法是先按任务内 rollout group 的 outcome reward 做 GRPO 式标准化，再把同一个 trajectory advantage 广播给所有 token。Mosaic 认为这样忽略了 session 使用效率，于是在“相同 outcome”内部再看 session count 的相对排序。直观上，若两条轨迹都成功，使用更少 session 的那条应得到更高 advantage；若两条都失败，反而不应简单惩罚 session 多的轨迹，因为失败样本仍需要探索空间。论文因此设计了一个有界调制项，用 session 数在同 reward 组内的 rank 去修正 trajectory-level advantage。这里有两个关键约束：一是调制不能打乱由 outcome reward 决定的主排序，二是调制幅度要受控，避免 session 偏好压过任务成败本身。作者强调它的作用不是替代 outcome signal，而是拉开 homogeneous-reward group 内部的 advantage 间距，提高学习信号分辨率。

第二层是 session-level advantage shaping。作者把每个 session 对最终 outcome 的边际贡献视作一种 immediate reward。做法上，是比较包含该 session 与不包含该 session 时的 outcome 增益，得到 session-level marginal gain；然后按 session type 分开做 group-relative normalization，再把这个 shaping signal 与上面的 trajectory-level advantage 结合。之所以要按 session type 分开归一化，是因为不同类型 session 的边际收益分布不同，例如压缩 session、主 agent session、fork 出来的子 agent session，其长度、功能和对最终成功率的贡献尺度都不一样，混在一起标准化会让某些类型的信号被系统性放大或压小。

整体上，Mosaic 形成了一个层级目标：trajectory-level signal 负责长期、全局、结果导向的优化；session-level shaping 负责局部、短程、边际贡献导向的优化。并且整个方法保持 critic-free，仍沿用 group-relative 的思路，而不是额外训练 value model。这是它和 PPO-style token/value advantage 路线的主要区别。76:T45f,This is not a pretraining paper in the narrow sense, but it matters for the pretrain-to-post-train interface, especially for long-context agents, tool-using systems, and reasoning models with explicit context management. Its contribution is meaningful in three ways. First, it treats session structure as part of the optimization problem rather than an implementation detail. That is important because modern agent execution increasingly departs from the single-context assumption used during RL training. Second, it proposes a hierarchical, critic-free advantage design, which fits the current preference for GRPO-like large-scale RL pipelines that avoid training an additional value model. Third, it explicitly encodes an efficiency preference: successful trajectories should ideally use fewer sessions, while unsuccessful ones should retain room for exploration. That idea is relevant beyond this benchmark, including memory agents and systems with context rewriting. Still, the scale of contribution is best viewed as a solid improvement in agent RL objective design, not a shift in core language model pretraining.77:T8d3,Mosaic introduces a two-level optimization signal.

The first component is session-aware trajectory-level advantage estimation. In the standard broadcasting setup, one computes a GRPO-style normalized trajectory advantage from outcome rewards within a rollout group, then assigns that same advantage to all tokens across all sessions. Mosaic argues that this ignores session efficiency. It therefore refines the trajectory-level signal using the relative ranking of session counts within trajectories that share the same outcome. Intuitively, if two trajectories both succeed, the one using fewer sessions should receive a larger advantage. If both fail, however, extra sessions should not be penalized in the same way because failed samples still serve exploration. The paper implements this through a bounded modulation term based on session-count ranking inside homogeneous-reward groups. Two design constraints are central: the modulation must not overturn the primary ordering induced by outcome reward, and its magnitude must remain controlled so that session preference does not dominate task success. The point is not to replace outcome supervision, but to increase advantage resolution within reward-tied groups.

The second component is session-level advantage shaping. Each session is assigned an immediate shaping signal based on its marginal contribution to the final outcome. Concretely, the method estimates a session-level marginal outcome gain, normalizes it with group-relative statistics separately for each session type, and combines this shaping term with the trajectory-level advantage. The type-conditioned normalization is important because different session types have different gain distributions. A compaction session, a main-agent session, and a forked subagent session differ in length, function, and contribution scale. Pooling them into one normalization scheme would distort the signal.

Together, these two components form a hierarchical objective: the trajectory-level term provides a global, long-horizon, outcome-oriented signal, while the session-level shaping term captures local marginal effects. The method remains critic-free throughout, staying closer to GRPO than to PPO-style value-based token advantage estimation.78:T6a1,Experiments are conducted on BrowseComp with Qwen3.5-4B as the base model, under two representative multi-session settings: context compaction and subagent forking. Mosaic outperforms both single-session and multi-session agentic RL baselines. The headline number is up to 10.1% relative accuracy improvement over the broadcasting baseline, while also reducing the average number of sessions per trajectory from 3.17 to 2.35. That matters because the gain is not coming from spending more sessions; it comes from better session utility and allocation.

Ablations show that both parts of the method matter. Removing the session-aware trajectory modulation reduces within-group advantage discrimination and hurts sample efficiency. Removing session-level shaping makes it harder for the policy to learn which sessions have real marginal value. The analysis section adds several useful observations:
1. Session-count-aware modulation increases advantage variance within same-reward groups, which helps when outcome rewards are too coarse and many samples tie.
2. Different session types indeed exhibit different marginal-gain distributions, validating the need for type-conditioned normalization.
3. Training changes the agent’s session usage pattern toward fewer but more useful sessions, suggesting that the objective shapes reasoning structure rather than merely adjusting token probabilities.
